💡 Key Takeaways
  • While it’s easy to get starstruck when working for an athlete or other high-profile client, Yohann Sangaré, an agent with eXp’s sports and entertainment division, discourages it.
  • Sangaré, a French former professional basketball player who played for 16 years across Europe, sometimes avoids reading up too much about his athlete clients’ accomplishments in their prospective sports so that he can focus on the task at hand: Finding them the right home and advising them on large investments.
  • when he was hired to work for Tony Parker, his former teammate, in San Antonio, Texas; he started as a financial advisor for professional athletes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While it’s easy to get starstruck when working for an athlete or other high-profile client, Yohann Sangaré, an agent with eXp’s sports and entertainment division, discourages it. “You come as a problem solver, not a fan,” he stated.

Sangaré, a French former professional basketball player who played for 16 years across Europe, sometimes avoids reading up too much about his athlete clients’ accomplishments in their prospective sports so that he can focus on the task at hand: Finding them the right home and advising them on large investments.

Sangaré came to the U.S. when he was hired to work for Tony Parker, his former teammate, in San Antonio, Texas; he started as a financial advisor for professional athletes. During COVID, he moved into real estate, specializing in finding homes for athletes instead.

In a recent development, sangaré explains that the pros tend to make a lot of money for a short period of time, and for that reason they’re usually interested in buying investment properties (often right after they’ve found homes for themselves and their family members). A big part of their real estate agents’ job, then, is to keep their eyes on investment properties with the potential for strong returns.

Sources indicate that athletes have specific needs. “As a rookie, they’re just starting out, and they may not want to buy,” Sangaré told Taylor Anderson at eXpcon in Salt Lake City last month. Depending on the length of the contract, a rental might be a better idea. “There are times you tell people now’s not the right time to buy. If they feel you’re working in their best interests, they will trust you,” mentioned Sangaré, who is part of eXp’s relatively newly introduced sports and entertainment division (which several brokerages offer).

You have to be patient when working with athletes, he said, since their situations are tied to ever-changing contracts; of course, players can be traded, and have to move swiftly. You also have to be prepared to wait and work with them as they grow in their careers.

What you don’t have to be: A major follower of their particular sports. Sangaré admits that as a European, he doesn’t know much about football or baseball, but that doesn’t stop him from working with athletes in those sports. Sometimes not being starstruck helps him work with a more level head, he stated.

But you do need to know the nuances of sports contracts. For example, some leagues, like the NBA, offer several-year guarantees, while others, like the NFL, don’t; housing options will vary based on those.

In a recent development, often the connection to an athlete client comes through their financial advisor or sports agent, Sangaré said. “The sports agent is always talking to the player, and he’ll know to reach out to you when someone gets traded,” he said.

But that can be a long road. Sangaré said it can take anywhere from five months to two years from starting a relationship with a sports agent to seeing any traction with a player, but you want to start that relationship early since once their clients do start to get traded, they’ll undoubtedly be approached by many other real estate agents. One practical tip he gives is going to the NBA Summer League in Las Vegas and taking agents out for coffee or lunch. “You have to be present where they’re present,” he said.

In a recent development, and when you do get connected to the client, make sure you don’t start with a sales pitch. “You can’t try to sell them something right away,” Sangaré stated; instead, you want to counsel them on how they can protect themselves and what they really need to know when buying a home — whether as an investment property or to live in.

The community-focused project illuminated a local gathering place ahead of the Christmas season, demonstrating how smart lighting can help bring people together.

BOWIE, Md., Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This holiday season, Linkind, a smart lighting brand specializing in connected lighting solutions, donated and installed permanent outdoor lights at Crossfire Worship Center in Bowie, Maryland.

It has been revealed that following installation, Linkind hosted a special lighting reveal at the church on Friday evening, bringing together members of the congregation and local community. Families counted down together and cheered as Linkind's holiday light show began. When the carolers started singing, bands of color moved across the church walls in time with the music. Neighbors joined in and shared warm drinks beneath the lights.

Christmas services bring families to Crossfire Worship Center during the holidays. In the months that follow, the same lights can welcome neighbors back for family gatherings and community events.

Industry observers note that as part of its holiday community initiative, Linkind provided Crossfire Worship Center with a complimentary outdoor lighting installation, helping transform the church's exterior into a welcoming illuminated space for its congregation and surrounding community. The lights are permanently mounted along the edge of the church roof, so the church can change its display each holiday without taking them down and rehanging them.

According to recent reports, the installation features Linkind's Smart Permanent Outdoor Lights ColorBlend System. Its dual-lens optical design casts overlapping bands of color on the church walls. The system offers 16 million colors, more than 120 preset lighting effects, and AI-assisted customization through the AiDot app. Church staff can use the app to switch the same fixtures from Christmas red and green to steady warm white above the entrance for an evening gathering.

"We're grateful for the opportunity to support Crossfire Worship Center by donating lights for this holiday display," remarked a spokesperson at Linkind. "We wanted to give something back to the Bowie community. We hope the finished display will be something the congregation and wider community can enjoy throughout the holiday season, and for years to come.".

If you are interested in Linkind's products, you can find them here:.

Linkind Smart Permanent Outdoor Lights ColorBlend | Dual Optics.

Linkind is a smart lighting brand offering solutions for home, outdoor, and entertainment spaces. Its portfolio includes smart bulbs, solar and landscape lighting, permanent outdoor lights, and immersive TV and gaming lighting.

It has been revealed that built on the belief that lighting should do more than illuminate, Linkind combines thoughtful design with intuitive controls and intelligent automation to make advanced lighting simple, reliable, and accessible. Its products bring everyday comfort, outdoor ambiance, and personalized entertainment experiences to homes worldwide.

Serving millions of users globally, Linkind is operated by AiDot Technology Inc., which designs, sells, and supports its products.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Darryl Davis Seminars Inc.’s multi-million dollar federal trademark infringement lawsuit against Epique Realty, which accuses the virtual brokerage of unlawfully using the POWER AGENT® brand in its nationwide operations, is headed to court next week.

During the first week of December, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Newly introduced York will hold a hearing on a motion for a preliminary injunction filed by Darryl Davis and his firm that would bar Epique Realty, a RealTrends Verified brokerage, from using the POWER AGENT trademark.

Sources indicate that originally filed in late June, the lawsuit alleges that Houston-based Epique Realty adopted the POWER AGENT name and “built an entire brand architecture around it” despite being put on notice and asked to stop, according to the announcement. In addition to Epique Realty, the lawsuit also lists Joshua Miller, Janice Delcid, Christopher Miller, XYZ Corps 1-10 and John and Jane Does 1-10 as defendants.

Darryl Davis Seminars notes it has used the POWER AGENT mark continuously since 1993 through The POWER Program, which it describes as the real estate industry’s oldest and longest-running agent training and coaching platform.

“POWER AGENT® has been our name since 1993, and both it and THE POWER PROGRAM® are registered trademarks,” Davis told HousingWire. “The law expects a trademark owner to protect its marks. We have for decades, and we will keep doing so. Because the matter is pending, I will let our court filings speak to the rest.”.

It has been revealed that in October, Epique filed a counterclaim asking for a ruling from the court that Davis’s trademark registrations of Power Agent programs do not give his firm exclusive rights to the word “power” and that this does not give Davis or his organization the rights to a family of “Power” trademarks. Epique is also asking the court to force Davis and his firm to prove likely confusing for each expression of “Power” Epique was accused of. Epique is also seeking rulings from the court that its current uses of PowerFlex and PowerCon, do not infringe on Davis’s trademarks and that it is not liable “merely because an independently controlled agent or third party used POWER-formative wording.”.

It has been revealed that epique emphasized in the filing that its agents are independent contractors and that the company does not hold passwords for agents’ personal social media accounts in order to edit or delete content, nor does it review agents’ social media posts or websites before they are published. This contradicts Davis’s complaint, which alleges that the brokerage’s independent contractor agreement requires agents to submit marketing or advertising posts for approval prior to publication. Additionally, the company mentioned that under state law in Texas, where Epique is headquartered, the firm is only responsible for ensuring that advertising content produced by agents complies with state rules.

It has been revealed that in a filing earlier this month, Davis largely denied Epique’s counterclaims, namely that he is trying to trademark the word “Power” by itself and he and his firm rejected Epique’s request that the court declares that Darryl Davis Seminars does not own the word “power” exclusively and that it does not have an across-the-board monopoly over trademarks containing the word. Throughout the filing, Davis maintained that Epique infringed on his firm’s trademarks and he asked the court to reject Epique’s counter claims.

This news was first reported by Inman. Epique Realty did not immediately returned HousingWire’s request for comment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that autonomous lawncare specialists Greenzie passed a major milestone with their self-driving mowers last week, surpassing 255,000 cumulative robomowing miles. For context, that’s far enough to mow every inch of space between the Earth and Moon.

Greenzie revealed the self-driving milestone last week, and it’s genuinely impressive, reflecting Greenzie Powered Autonomy mowing more than 9 billion (with a b) square feet of turf across more than 200 commercial customers, 45 US states, and more than 500,000 equivalent man-hours of mowing.

And, while I might have pointed the fact that Greenzie mowers have covered more miles in its press release than Daimler’s entire hydrogen truck fleet, the organization really seems to be leaning into the Moon angle.

According to recent reports, “We mowed to the moon, but the real achievement is the commercial experience behind those miles,” states Charles Brian Quinn, co-founder and CEO of Greenzie and almost definitely the guy who first came up with the lunar lawncare line. “Every mile represents equipment working on real properties with commercial crews. That experience has shaped our technology, strengthened our OEM partnerships and taught us how to help customers successfully integrate autonomy into their daily operations.”.

In a recent development, greenzie develops autonomous packages for, and maintains OEM relationships with electric brands Mean Green Electric Mowers (whose Vanquish Autonomous commercial mower is shown, above), and Greenworks Commercial, as well as gas-powered brands like Bobcat and Wright Manufacturing. Regardless of what powers the mowers, Greenzie supplies the self-driving technology and integration expertise, while its OEM partners develop and manufacture the equipment that does the actual cutting, clearing, and whatever else their clients need.

“Successful autonomy requires more than capable technology,” said Steve Bush, chief operating officer of Greenzie. “Customers need to understand where autonomy fits into their operations, how to prepare their crews and how to measure success. We have spent years learning those lessons alongside our customers and OEM partners, creating a more consistent path to adoption as the industry grows.”.

The Mean Green Vanquish Autonomous featured gere is a fully electric, stand-on, zero-turn (ZTR) mower built around an all-day-ready 22 kWh li-ion battery pack and featuring a 60″ rear-discharge mulching deck.

Mean Green claims that the combination of massive battery and the electric motors that drive the ZTR mower and spin up its blades are good up to eight hours of continuous mowing on a charge, with an aluminum chassis and deck helping to keep the machine’s overall weight down for easier towing maximum efficiency.

The firm states the mower can operate in either manual or autonomous mode, with Greenzie’s self-driving software supported by six depth-sensing stereo cameras providing 360-degree vision, RTK-corrected GPS, and visual-inertial odometry for onboard site mapping and precise positioning, which Greenzie says allows the mower to detect obstacles up to twenty feet away, recognize designated keep-out zones, and automatically return to its starting point when called back.

A top speed of 11.5 mph and the ability to repeat saved mowing routes, the Vanquish is designed to give commercial landscaping crews another productive worker without adding another person to the payroll … which, with a $60,000 asking price, is money they will probably still need.

Let’s get some pro-labor rage going in the comments, and don’t forget to mention what kind of paycheck you’d need to get to go work in landscaping 2,000+ hours a year while you’re there.

Tech Report: Dell and HP beat expectations, but their fortunes are diverging as AI dynamics crush the PC market

💡 Key Takeaways
  • delivered strong earnings and revenue beats as they posted their latest financial results today.
  • However, the companies have very different prospects going forward as they try to come to terms with the diverging fortunes of the artificial intelligence server and personal computer markets they serve.
  • Dell reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $9.45 per share on revenue of $54.94 billion, a stunning result that blew past Wall Street’s expectations of just $6.59 per share in earnings and $49.32 billion in sales.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:48 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Updated with Wednesday stock prices:.

Dell Technologies Inc. and HP Inc. delivered strong earnings and revenue beats as they posted their latest financial results today.

However, the companies have very different prospects going forward as they try to come to terms with the diverging fortunes of the artificial intelligence server and personal computer markets they serve.

Dell reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $9.45 per share on revenue of $54.94 billion, a stunning result that blew past Wall Street’s expectations of just $6.59 per share in earnings and $49.32 billion in sales.

According to recent reports, the organization’s revenue more than doubled from a year earlier thanks to the sky-high demand for the AI servers and related data center infrastructure equipment it sells. Dell’s Infrastructure Solutions Group delivered sales of $41.97 billion during the quarter, far in excess of the Street’s target of $35.27 billion. Of that, around $22 billion came from direct AI-optimized server sales, the company noted. That segment was up 291% annually.

In a recent development, “We are now a different firm, with the Infrastructure Solutions Group driving the vast majority of our profit and growth,” remarked Dell Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke (pictured). He added that Dell now has more than 7,500 customers buying its AI servers.

The Street liked what it saw, with Dell’s stock rising more than 3% after hours, putting the brakes on an 11% decline earlier, during the regular trading session. Enhancement: However, on another down day for tech stocks Wednesday, Dell’s shares were falling almost 8% before the market cut some of those losses and Dell was falling only a fraction of a point.

Dell’s performance in the quarter sets a fresh precedent for infrastructure systems companies, stated longtime technology industry analyst Dave Vellante, chief analyst at theCUBE Research, SiliconANGLE Media’s sister market research firm.

Industry observers note that “Dell has transformed from a PC manufacturer into a dominant enterprise infrastructure provider and industry bellwether,” he said. “What’s most astounding to me is that I’ve always considered AWS to be Dell’s most formidable competitor. Dell is now significantly larger than AWS on a trailing 12-month revenue basis and is growing at a rate that’s more than double that of AWS, Azure and on a par with Google Cloud.”.

Dell is raising its forecast for AI servers in the coming fiscal years, and now sees sales rising to a staggering $78 billion, ahead of the Street’s target of $74 billion. At present, the manufacturer has an even bigger order backlog of $132.3 billion for AI servers. “Every order is verified for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance and access to land and power,” Clarke told analysts in response to a question about the reliability of that backlog.

Vellante remarked Dell’s operating leverage is just as impressive, with its operating income, net profit and earnings per share all growing at rates over two-times its revenue growth.

In a recent development, “Its massive backlog and strong product execution allow it to be selective,” the analyst remarked. “Thus the quality of its revenue and its backlog is very high, and the firm is well-positioned for the next several quarters. Current market signals point to a structural change in tech where vendors that are in a position to help customers transform and drive latest levels of productivity are poised to win over the long term. We increasingly see Dell as one of those leaders.”.

Besides servers, Dell still has a big business in the PC market. Its Client Services Group was once the company’s biggest segment, but its revenue is now dwarfed by AI server sales. During the quarter, it generated revenue of $12.89 billion, below the Street’s forecast of $14.33 billion.

In a recent development, the reason for that miss is that the global PC market is right now enduring a sharp decline. Last month, Gartner Inc. reported a stunning 22% drop in global PC shipments in the third quarter, citing the increased costs of components such as memory chips, which have led to higher prices and compelled many people to hold onto their older laptops for longer.

The miserable state of PC sales makes HP’s latest quarterly results seem even more impressive than they were. However, the manufacturer’s cautious outlook suggests that its incoming Chief Executive Emma Walmsley (pictured, right) will have her work cut out when she assumes the role full time on Jan. 4, when she’s slated to take over from interim CEO Bruce Broussard.

Recent findings suggest that HP reported fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of 83 cents per share, surpassing the analyst consensus estimate that called for a profit of just 75 cents per share. Revenue for the period came to $16 billion, up 9% and above the Street’s target of $15.4 billion.

In a recent development, HP’s stock briefly surged more than 17% after-hours, before promptly surrendering all of those gains in under an hour. It was down just under a percentage point at the time of writing. Upgrade: On Wednesday, investors appeared to change their minds again, as the stock was rising more than 12%.

Recent findings suggest that investors had low expectations of HP given the shoddy state of the PC market. The company has been trying to mitigate the situation somewhat by raising its prices, but it couldn’t stop its profit margins from declining in the quarter.

The market was eagerly anticipating HP’s guidance to try and get a lid on whether or not the PC market has any prospect of recovery in the near future, but the organization disappointed by refusing to provide any. All it would say is that it forecasts free cash flow in the current quarter to be $3 billion, plus or minus $100 million. Analysts are targeting free cash flow of $3.3 billion.

It has been revealed that HP hasn’t been helped by the fact that it has been without a CEO since PayPal Holdings Inc. surprisingly swooped in to poach its former leader Enrique Lores in February. Broussard has held the fort for close to nine months now, but the company did at least finally name a successor in Walmsley, who will begin her tenure next year. She formerly led the pharmaceutical giant GSK Plc.

Breaking: FutureMain Sets Its Sights on Nasdaq, Bringing Decades of Industrial Expertise Into the AI Era

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The South Korean industrial AI company combines 38 years of engineering expertise with explainable artificial intelligence, targeting the next generation of intelligent manufacturing.
  • 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FutureMain, a South Korean industrial artificial intelligence company specializing in machinery diagnostics and predictive and prescriptive maintenance, is pursuing a Nasdaq listing as part of its strategy to expand into global manufacturing markets.
  • On September 11, 2026, FutureMain declared that it had entered into a definitive business combination agreement with ChampionsGate Acquisition Corp., a Nasdaq-listed special purpose acquisition tech giant (SPAC).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The South Korean industrial AI company combines 38 years of engineering expertise with explainable artificial intelligence, targeting the next generation of intelligent manufacturing.

SUWON, South Korea, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FutureMain, a South Korean industrial artificial intelligence company specializing in machinery diagnostics and predictive and prescriptive maintenance, is pursuing a Nasdaq listing as part of its strategy to expand into global manufacturing markets.

On September 11, 2026, FutureMain declared that it had entered into a definitive business combination agreement with ChampionsGate Acquisition Corp., a Nasdaq-listed special purpose acquisition tech giant (SPAC).

In a recent development, upon completion of the proposed transaction, the combined organization is expected to be listed on Nasdaq. The parties anticipate closing the transaction in 2027, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals and other customary closing conditions.

Recent findings suggest that for FutureMain, the proposed listing represents more than an opportunity to raise its international profile. It is a strategic step toward building the scale, operational capacity and global service infrastructure required to serve major industrial customers.

Recent findings suggest that deploying latest technologies across large manufacturing facilities and mission-critical production systems requires more than technical performance. Global manufacturers also demand long-term business continuity, dependable delivery capabilities and confidence in their technology partners.

By pursuing access to the U.S. capital markets, FutureMain aims to strengthen its international business foundation and accelerate the adoption of its industrial AI technologies.

The ambition is substantial for a tech giant that began with just three people and had approximately 24 employees in early 2026.

Yet the manufacturer's vision is rooted in a problem that manufacturers around the world have faced for generations: understanding why machines fail â and preventing those failures before they disrupt operations.

Before Machines Fail, They Send Signals.

When a major manufacturing facility unexpectedly shuts down, the consequences can extend far beyond the factory floor.

Automotive production lines, pharmaceutical plants, power generation facilities and shipyards all depend on complex machinery operating reliably, often around the clock.

And before many mechanical failures occur, equipment begins to exhibit subtle changes.

A vibration too faint for the human ear to detect. A temperature variation that is difficult to observe directly. An unusual pattern hidden within operational data.

For decades, experienced maintenance engineers have relied on specialized knowledge and practical experience to interpret these signals.

But what if artificial intelligence could learn to apply the diagnostic expertise accumulated by engineers over generations?

What if industrial equipment could be monitored not simply to detect abnormal conditions, but to identify emerging risks, explain their underlying causes and recommend appropriate maintenance actions?

That is the future FutureMain is working to create.

Turning 38 Years of Engineering Knowledge Into Industrial AI.

The global artificial intelligence industry is advancing rapidly, with companies competing to develop increasingly capable models and applications.

Yet applying AI effectively in real industrial environments remains a fundamentally different challenge.

A factory cannot be fully understood through information learned from the internet alone.

Similar vibration patterns may indicate entirely different mechanical problems depending on equipment design, operating conditions and the physical mechanisms involved.

For plant operators, an alarm indicating that something is abnormal is rarely sufficient to justify stopping a critical production line.

What matters is understanding not only what is wrong, but why it is happening and what should be done next.

FutureMain developed its flagship ExRBM platform to address precisely this challenge.

Founded in 2014, the tech giant has incorporated 38 years of accumulated machinery diagnostic engineering expertise from power plants, industrial facilities and manufacturing environments into its AI-based technologies.

ExRBM combines expert knowledge of mechanical failure mechanisms with machine learning, deep learning and actual equipment data.

Rather than relying solely on statistical anomaly detection, the platform is designed to identify specific failure mechanisms, explain the evidence behind its assessments and recommend appropriate responses.

According to manufacturer disclosures, ExRBM can automatically identify more than 85 machinery failure mechanisms, including bearing damage and shaft misalignment.

In 100 tests conducted by the Korea Testing Laboratory (KTL), the technology recorded a reported automatic diagnostic accuracy of 98.3% under the specified test conditions.

FutureMain also reports 25 patents and international recognition, including a gold medal at the International Exhibition of Inventions Geneva.

The company believes its most important advantage, however, cannot be measured by the speed at which an algorithm is developed.

It lies in the depth of engineering knowledge embedded within that algorithm.

Decades of experience analyzing normal equipment behavior, abnormal operating conditions and mechanical failures have produced a specialized body of knowledge that is difficult to replicate through software development alone.

By transforming this expertise into AI-driven diagnostic capabilities, FutureMain aims to make advanced industrial knowledge more accessible, scalable and actionable.

Proven Across Industries, From Battery Manufacturing to Shipbuilding.

Industrial AI must ultimately demonstrate its value where it matters most: in operating manufacturing facilities.

FutureMain's technologies have been deployed across more than 10 industrial sectors, including battery manufacturing, pharmaceuticals and biotechnology, power generation, energy, shipbuilding and defense.

Its customer references include LG Energy Solution, Hanwha Ocean and Handok.

According to the organization's 2026 investor presentation, ExRBM recorded 25 deployments over the preceding three years, while FutureMain's total customer base exceeded 48 companies.

Several customer relationships have also progressed beyond initial deployments.

At Handok's Eumseong pharmaceutical manufacturing facility, applications have expanded from equipment predictive maintenance into the integration of production-process data and quality anomaly detection across granulation, coating and tablet-compression processes.

At Hanwha Ocean, machinery diagnostic applications have been extended to additional equipment following earlier system installations.

FutureMain's collaboration with LG Energy Solution is also moving toward broader applications across domestic and overseas manufacturing operations.

The tech giant is expanding into robotics as well.

In 2026, FutureMain has been carrying out a large-scale predictive maintenance implementation project involving welding robots and traversing equipment at HD Hyundai Construction Equipment's Ulsan facility.

These developments reflect the manufacturer's transition from solving individual machinery problems toward building an industrial AI platform applicable across different equipment types, production processes and manufacturing sectors.

International expansion is another area of focus.

FutureMain reports that it has completed a proof-of-concept evaluation at a Saudi Aramco facility and is extending its business network across the Middle East, Southeast Asia and Japan.

From its origins in Suwon, South Korea, the company is positioning its industrial AI technology for a broader role in global manufacturing.

ExRBM 2.0: Moving From Monitoring to Explainable Intelligence.

In November 2026, FutureMain introduced ExRBM 2.0 at an AIoT technology presentation held at COEX in Seoul.

The next-generation platform represents an evolution from conventional equipment monitoring toward AI-assisted diagnosis and maintenance decision-making.

Traditional monitoring systems typically generate alerts when vibration, temperature or other operating parameters exceed predefined thresholds.

ExRBM 2.0 takes a more advanced approach.

By analyzing collected equipment data, the platform is designed to identify potential faults, explain their underlying causes and recommend appropriate maintenance actions.

A central feature is explainable artificial intelligence, or XAI, which allows owners to examine the reasoning and evidence supporting an AI-generated diagnosis.

This distinction is particularly important in industrial environments.

When a critical machine is at risk of failure, engineers cannot always act on an unexplained warning.

They need to understand the nature of the suspected defect, the relevant frequency characteristics, the location or timing of abnormal signals and the maintenance actions that may be required.

By providing this context, ExRBM 2.0 aims to support more informed and confident decision-making.

FutureMain has also presented capabilities connecting machinery diagnostics with remaining useful life (RUL) estimation, maintenance work orders and automated diagnostic reporting.

RUL estimation is applicable depending on equipment characteristics and the availability and quality of relevant data.

In addition, the organization has introduced the concept of an AI assistant based on a small language model (sLLM), enabling people to interact with machinery information and maintenance records through natural-language queries.

Instead of manually navigating multiple diagnostic screens, an engineer could ask:.

"What problem has been detected in this machine?".

"Which component should be inspected first?".

"How should we determine the appropriate maintenance timing?".

The objective is not to replace experienced engineers.

It is to preserve, transfer and extend their specialized knowledge, allowing more industrial professionals to benefit from advanced diagnostic expertise.

Beyond Predictive Maintenance: AI That Understands the Entire Factory.

FutureMain's long-term strategy extends well beyond machinery diagnostics.

The manufacturer is pursuing a manufacturing-focused vertical AI platform that connects equipment health, production processes, quality management and robotics.

Modern manufacturing facilities generate enormous volumes of data, including machinery vibration, electrical current, temperature, process pressure, equipment load and quality inspection results.

When these data sources are analyzed independently, manufacturers may identify isolated problems without understanding their broader operational relationships.

FutureMain sees an opportunity to connect them.

By integrating equipment-condition data with production and quality information, industrial AI could move beyond detecting individual machinery faults to understanding more complex interactions across manufacturing operations.

The manufacturer's longer-term vision includes industrial AI agents capable of interpreting factory-wide conditions, analyzing operational risks and recommending appropriate responses.

Robotics represents another potential growth area.

As industrial robots become more widely deployed, technologies capable of diagnosing their mechanical condition and identifying emerging failure patterns may become increasingly key.

FutureMain is conducting research into technologies that learn normal and abnormal robotic operating patterns, on-device AI and Physical AI applications tailored to industrial environments.

Some of these initiatives remain in research and development.

Nevertheless, the company's strategic direction is clear: to build on its established machinery diagnostic expertise and expand toward AI systems that understand manufacturing processes, product quality and the increasingly interconnected relationship between humans and robots.

A Vision Built on Real-World Expertise.

The ultimate purpose of industrial AI is not defined solely by the complexity of its algorithms or the number of patents behind it.

Its value can be found in more fundamental outcomes.

Helping prevent unexpected machinery shutdowns.

Supporting safer working environments.

Enabling more informed decisions where experienced specialists are in short supply.

And helping manufacturers produce the goods that society depends on with greater reliability.

While much of the world's attention is focused on the latest advances in generative AI, FutureMain believes the physical signals produced by industrial machinery remain an essential source of intelligence.

Behind those signals are decades of engineering knowledge and practical experience.

Shine Lee, FutureMain's Chief Operating Officer and a founding member who joined the organization when it consisted of just three people, believes that this foundation will become increasingly key as the AI market matures.

According to recent reports, "Today, countless AI-powered products and services are being created, only to disappear as rapidly as they emerge," Lee said. "AI services without deep technological foundations can easily be replaced by similar offerings. In an increasingly crowded AI market, what truly matters is building AI on technologies and expertise that cannot be easily replicated.".

Lee emphasized the importance of connecting artificial intelligence with the physical realities of manufacturing.

"Understanding real industrial equipment requires going directly into factories, examining machinery, installing sensors and collecting reliable physical data," she mentioned. "The ability to acquire that data and transform it into meaningful intelligence for AI-driven decision-making is what FutureMain does best. It is also the foundation of our long-term competitive advantage.".

Looking ahead, Lee described a vision that extends beyond traditional engineering AI.

"Our ambition is to evolve into a Hyperconnected Autonomous AI company â one where data from across the factory is seamlessly interconnected, enabling manufacturing operations to pursue optimal efficiency and continuous self-improvement.".

This vision reflects FutureMain's belief that the next generation of industrial AI will be defined not simply by more powerful models, but by deeper integration with the physical world.

Building the Next Generation of Industrial Intelligence.

FutureMain's journey, supported by 38 years of accumulated engineering expertise and a team of approximately 24 employees in early 2026, is moving beyond South Korea toward new opportunities in global manufacturing.

The proposed Nasdaq listing could represent an notable milestone in that journey.

Yet the firm's larger ambition is not defined by a stock market valuation.

It is rooted in the belief that AI capable of understanding real industrial environments can contribute to safer workplaces, more productive factories and a more resilient manufacturing ecosystem.

Around the world, millions of machines continue to operate inside factories, power plants, shipyards and industrial facilities.

Each generates signals that reveal something about its condition.

FutureMain is working to transform those signals into actionable intelligence â connecting decades of engineering expertise with the capabilities of modern AI.

The future of manufacturing may depend not only on making machines more intelligent, but on giving artificial intelligence a deeper understanding of the physical world.

And for FutureMain, that future is already taking shape on the factory floor.

Industry News: Sometimes the most valuable data is the house nobody bought

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (827 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, want to price more precisely?
  • In a recent development, when agents sit down to price a listing, we know the drill: Pull the solds.
  • But there’s another category of data sitting right there in the MLS that we frequently overlook: the houses nobody bought.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, want to price more precisely? Canceled listing data in the MLS can reveal where buyers remarked no. Learn three steps to add failed listings to your next CMA.

In a recent development, when agents sit down to price a listing, we know the drill: Pull the solds. Look at what’s coming soon, active and pending. Adjust for condition, location, square footage and amenities. Figure out where our house fits.

But there’s another category of data sitting right there in the MLS that we frequently overlook: the houses nobody bought.

According to recent reports, expired. Canceled. Withdrawn. Earlier in my career, I looked at these failed listings all the time. Then the market changed. When inventory became tight, and buyers were competing for homes, digging through failed listings often wasn’t necessary to determine where a property would sell.

Now the market is shifting again; pricing must be more precise, and I’m sharpening my approach by bringing an old tool back into my pricing process.

A sold comp tells us where a buyer noted yes, but a failed listing can help us figure out where buyers said no. And in a buyer-favored market, that’s valuable information.

Recent findings suggest that imagine you’re pricing a home, and the recent comparable sales range from $600,000 to $625,000. Then you expand your search.

Recent findings suggest that suddenly, you know considerably more than the sold comps alone told you. Other sellers have already tested the upper limits of pricing, and buyers responded. It’s essentially a series of pricing experiments someone else conducted for you — and they paid the carrying costs.

One of the most interesting things buried in MLS history is the pricing journey. A property might show a final list price of $649,000 and an eventual sale of $630,000. Dig deeper, and you may discover this:.

$725,000 → $699,000 → $675,000 → canceled → relisted at $649,000 → sold for $630,000.

That’s a different story. The sale tells us what one buyer eventually paid. The listing history tells us buyers had previously rejected that house at $725,000, $699,000 and $675,000.

According to recent reports, it also illustrates something sellers don’t always understand: Getting to the right price eventually isn’t necessarily the same as pricing correctly from the beginning. After months of market exposure and multiple reductions, buyers may stop asking, “Could this be the house?” They start asking, “What’s wrong with it?”.

Sources indicate that when I find a comparable property that sat for 90 days without selling, I want to know what did sell during those same 90 days. Sometimes we blame the market when the market was functioning just fine. Buyers were buying houses. They simply weren’t buying that one.

Maybe they chose the renovated house at $640,000. Maybe they paid $650,000 for the better lot. They may have even paid more for another property because it offered something the failed listing didn’t. That’s useful information when you’re sitting across from a seller who believes buyers just need more time to appreciate their home.

If buyers repeatedly toured the property and purchased competing homes instead, the market may already have delivered its opinion.

This is where agents have to resist oversimplifying the data. An expired listing isn’t automatic proof that a house was overpriced, and a canceled listing certainly isn’t either.

Listings fail for all sorts of reasons. Sellers change their minds. Job transfers fall through. Repairs surface. Agents get fired. Sometimes a seller receives a perfectly acceptable offer and decides not to move.

In a recent development, so, investigate. Call the previous agent. I might simply say:.

Sources indicate that “I’m pricing a similar property and noticed yours was on the market last year. Is there anything you can tell me about the activity or why the seller decided not to continue?”.

Sources indicate that twenty-seven showings and no offers tell me something. Two showings in four months tells me something different.

There’s one more number worth considering: the cost of the pricing journey.

Find a house that started high, sat, reduced, expired, relisted and eventually sold. Then compare it with similar homes that entered the market closer to where buyers were actually buying.

Recent findings suggest that sellers often view aspirational pricing as a no-risk strategy: “We can always come down.” Technically, that’s true. But time isn’t free, and neither is market perception.

The next time you’re preparing a CMA in a shifting or buyer-favored market:.

Industry observers note that we’re very good at studying success in real estate. But as pricing gets harder, I’ve found myself returning to an old habit: studying the failures, too. Sold listings tell us where buyers have been willing to say yes. Sometimes the house nobody bought is the one that tells us exactly where they started saying no.

Roxanne Hale is the associate broker of the Art House Team, brokered by RealtySouth in Birmingham, Alabama. Get connected on Facebook or YouTube.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.

Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.

Industry observers note that surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong? Or is it?

After Tesla’s “We, Robot” event in October 2024, Brownlee (MKBHD) noted there was no way Tesla would deliver a Cybercab to a customer for $30,000 or less before 2027. If it did, he’d shave his head on camera.

Industry observers note that musk has taken it personally ever since. When the first Cybercab came off the Giga Texas line in February, he replied “Gonna happen 😂” to a bald-MKBHD meme, which we covered at the time. In September, after Brownlee doubled down in a latest video, Musk wrote: “I guess he really wants to shave his head 🤷‍♂️”.

On Friday, Tesla started inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use. The order page lists $29,990, a mandatory $299 per month Autonomy Subscription, a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, and an estimated delivery of December 2026, only in Tesla’s Texas Robotaxi cities.

Sources indicate that as we reported Friday, the car only operates inside Tesla’s Robotaxi geofences. And Tesla’s Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement says it “will not operate” without the $299 proposal, bans owners from putting it on the Robotaxi network or using it for ride-hailing, and lets Tesla shrink the operating area at any time.

So Tesla designed a robotaxi, then offered it to select private owners who aren’t allowed to use it as a taxi. Over five years, that’s $47,631 before insurance, registration, and charging. And you are limited to small geofenced areas. If you stop paying Tesla’s monthly fee, which it can change at all times, your cybercab becomes a paperweight.

Brownlee laid out his case Friday night. There are no deliveries yet, the car is invite-only rather than publicly available, and it can’t be used as a cab outside of the existing geofences. He called it “a paperweight if I take this thing home,” though he admits that last point isn’t technically part of the bet.

Industry observers note that the memes are everywhere, so let’s go back over the bet: Cybercab publicly available for under $30k by the end of 2026My hair is safe for several reasons1: No deliveries yet. But they’re estimating starting in December so that’s neat2: Invite only, not actually publicly… https://t.co/NCD2aFbe2c.

Tesla fans fired back with clips from his September video, where he described a car that “will not ship to regular people like you and me for $30k before the end of 2026.” Whole Mars Catalog, an Elon Musk propagandist whose real name is Omar Qazi, told him to “be a man and honor your word.” Musk reposted it, then replied:.

Musk also reposted a Grok answer claiming the current offer “matches” the conditions of the bet.

But around the same time, Musk replied directly to Brownlee’s post about the order page, and it didn’t help Tesla’s case:.

Sources indicate that “It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval. But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.”.

That’s Tesla’s CEO confirming, a day after launch, that the car can’t be sold outside the areas where it already operates and that its price is wrong. A price that Musk fully controls.

Yes, it looks like Tesla is rushing this out just to win a bet against a Youtuber. Absolutely insane behavior. We’ve seen this movie before. In June 2025, Tesla did a single “autonomous delivery” of a Model Y to meet a Musk deadline, then never did it again.

According to recent reports, tesla always pitched the Cybercab as a vehicle for its Robotaxi network. Now, seven weeks before the deadline, a personal-use version shows up that’s invite-only, Texas-only, banned from doing the one thing it was designed for, and attached to a subscription Musk himself says is too expensive. If you set out to build a product whose main job was letting Musk claim he won a Twitter bet, it would look a lot like this.

According to recent reports, this Cybercab offering is completely broken. The value proposition is awful. As others have put it, it’s a permanent variable rate lease starting at $300 a month with a ridiculous $30,000 down payment.

Besides, the bet was "under 30k." Starting price is under 30k, but a subscription is required, which takes it over 30k, just to use it for one day. They could have given the car away for free, and just charged a fee to use it. Doesn't change the total cost.

In a recent development, what do you get for this deal? A 2-seater vehicle that only works in small, incomplete, geo-fenced areas and has no steering wheel to do anything else with it. Meanwhile, Tesla insists that the Model Y, like the ones used in its current Robotaxi service alongside the Cybercab, uses the same self-driving technology.

You can buy one for $40,000, and you get a lot more car than the Cybercab; then you can pay $99 a month for FSD instead of $300 a month. Tesla is supposed to let current Tesla owners drive without supervision in the geo-fenced areas, which would basically be the same product as what Tesla is offering right now with the Cybertruck, but you are not a slave to Tesla, which can brick your car at any time or change the terms.

This offer simply makes no sense, and Musk is sort of admitting it by saying the price should be the same as FSD, not $300 a month.

#134553. Industry News: BOXABL financial filing shows cash burn and scaling risk

General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: BOXABL financial filing shows cash burn and scaling risk

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2310 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • [Editor’s note: HousingWire TBD author Dan Oppenheim contributed financial analysis and insight for this report.].
  • Factory-built housing’s promise of a not-so-distant brighter future has always been compelling.
  • Forever, it seems, it has carried an “always within five years” sense of inevitability, stuck in limbo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[Editor’s note: HousingWire TBD author Dan Oppenheim contributed financial analysis and insight for this report.].

Factory-built housing’s promise of a not-so-distant brighter future has always been compelling.

Forever, it seems, it has carried an “always within five years” sense of inevitability, stuck in limbo. Build homes faster, with less waste, fewer labor constraints, greater consistency, in conditioned indoor offsite space, and at costs low enough to bend asking-price curves toward households priced out of homeownership.

The arrival of housing’s future, however, seems caught in the unforgiving calculus of time and space’s infinite divisibility. Progress happens and promises soar, but the ultimate goal of powering United States home development and construction with modern manufacturing going concerns keeps falling short, trapped in an echo chamber of not-exactly-here and not-quite-yet.

It has been revealed that the rub has always been turning the promise of housing’s future into a business that can reliably produce homes, deliver them to customers, cover its costs, and generate enough cash to keep doing it. Many homebuilding business leaders who’ve tried a lot of things and kept doing what works are apt to think of all that as homebuilding’s never-ending siren’s song, one that, should it emerge, should be dispelled as a wishful-thinking distraction.

BOXABL, the Las Vegas-based modular housing manufacturer that completed its Nasdaq listing in July, now faces that test amid mounting difficulties, including self-inflicted ones.

Its November 16, 2026, quarterly filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission provides data to address questions that experienced homebuilding executives have long raised about factory-based housing ventures and that they have expressed about BOXABLE.

According to recent reports, can a manufacturer achieve sufficient production volume to absorb fixed costs? Can it coordinate factory output with site readiness, permitting, installation, and customer financing? And can it sustain those operations when capital is expensive, construction inputs remain inflation-pressured, and affordability-constrained homebuyers are wavering for any of half a dozen good reasons?

It has been revealed that BOXABL’s filing shows progress in generating orders. It also shows that the company’s operating model still falls far short of demonstrating the economic soundness, scalability, and durability required to sustain a residential construction business. The company’s options have not disappeared, but they have narrowed, and time is quickly passing. Management has less room and less time to demonstrate the business’s financial sustainability.

BOXABL’s Form 10-Q, filed on November 16 for the quarter ended September 30, reports $14 million in unrestricted cash, down from $29 million at year-end 2025. During the most recent quarter, the tech giant used $6 million in cash for operations, down from $8.4 million in the third quarter of 2025. This translates to a cash burn rate of about $2 million per month, so the $14 million of unrestricted cash on hand as of the end of Q3 represents seven months of operations.

That metric doesn’t precisely forecast when BOXABL might run out of cash. Instead, it reveals the relationship between available resources and BOXABL’s most recent cash-burn rate.

In Note 4 of the filing, the company states: “Substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern exists.”.

Is the disclosure a prediction of failure? Technically and officially, no. Management identifies continued cost controls, accelerated Casita deliveries and sales, and additional equity financing as measures intended to address the uncertainty. There’s no ambiguity that those measures must deliver results even as the tech giant continues to consume cash.

Industry observers note that BOXABL reported 209 net orders for Casitas in Q3, bringing its total for the first nine months to 362 net orders. As of September 30, the company had 679 Casitas in backlog, representing approximately $45 million in potential revenue. Those figures indicate customer interest but raise what are arguably the most important questions for BOXABL – how legitimate the orders are, how much of the backlog will convert to revenue, and when that conversion will occur.

The point is that while most homebuilders count a signed contract as an order only after the customer has satisfied mortgage qualification, BOXABL notes that 85 Casitas in the backlog (and recorded as an order during a recent quarter) are pending feasibility studies to assess whether the customer’s site can support installation.

Sources indicate that in addition, another 311 units in the backlog were associated with orders that were one to two years old, raising questions about whether they will convert to revenue. Together, these 396 units, the 85 units that still require feasibility assessment, and the 311 older orders represent 58% of the tech giant’s reported backlog of 679 units.

That disconnect is not merely a scheduling matter. Backlog becomes financially meaningful only when orders reliably convert to completed sales. For BOXABL, that conversion process remains insufficiently demonstrated, likely raising investor doubts about the authenticity of the orders and the cleanliness of the backlog.

During the first nine months of 2026, BOXABL generated $2.629 million in revenue, up from $588,000 a year earlier. It delivered 36 Casitas, compared with eight in the prior-year period. However, cost of goods sold totaled $13.78 million, resulting in a gross loss of $11.15 million.

Approximately $10 million of those costs were inventory valuation adjustments and allowances for slow-moving or obsolete inventory. These accounting charges should not be mistaken for the direct manufacturing cost of the 36 delivered units. Nevertheless, they reflect the economic consequences of producing and carrying inventory that would not generate sufficient revenue.

Looking at BOXABL’s production costs, excluding obsolete inventory, inventory adjustments, scrapped inventory, warranty expense, and allocations such as stock-based compensation expense, the tech giant reported a cost of Casitas sold of $2.075 million for the first nine months of the year, compared with $2.629 million in revenue, leaving an adjusted gross profit of approximately $550,000.

Recent findings suggest that however, when assessing BOXABL’s ability to produce Casitas at a profit, it’s difficult to ignore the message and significance of the largest component of the inventory charge, $7.4 million, which represented an adjustment to reduce the carrying value of the inventory to its realizable value. Although that charge affects more inventory than was sold in the first nine months of 2026, it is unclear whether BOXABL’s newly produced inventory would sell at or above its cost of production.

BOXABL is not at the moment scaled – from a management perspective – for this low level of volume and revenue. Its $2.629 million in revenue for the first nine months of 2026 was dwarfed by $15.553 million in operating expenses, which included general and administrative expenses, sales and marketing, and research and development. BOXABL has developed a product and a manufacturing system.

By any measure, however, its reported results have not yet demonstrated that the system can operate at volumes and margins sufficient to sustain it.

It has been revealed that perhaps the most revealing figures concern inventory. At September 30, BOXABL reported $17.645 million in inventory for 388 units, including 198 finished Casitas and 190 work-in-process units. While this inventory balance may not sound like much, it represents 6.7x the revenue generated during the first nine months of 2026. That $17.645 million of inventory is also after adjustments (write-downs), as the cost to produce the inventory was $10 million higher.

Management explains that significant finished inventory remains on hand because customer sites are not ready for delivery and installation. Delays stem from feasibility studies, permitting, land preparation, and other deployment requirements. That disclosure addresses a problem that residential construction executives understand.

Sources indicate that manufacturing a housing unit is only one part of delivering a completed home. Factory efficiencies cannot eliminate the complexities of land preparation, local regulations, logistics, installation, and customer financing.

When manufacturing and delivery schedules diverge, capital remains tied up in products that cannot yet generate revenue. Inventory must be stored, managed, and sometimes modified to meet changing specifications. BOXABL’s filing reports that approximately $7.1 million of finished goods was reclassified as work in process in 2025 to accommodate modifications for California’s modular housing requirements.

It has been revealed that none of this establishes that the manufacturing approach cannot work. It highlights that the economic benefits of industrialized construction must be measured across the entire housing delivery process, not merely the time or labor required to assemble a unit in a factory.

Sources indicate that notably, BOXABL revealed that on October 27th, it signed a contract to sell 20 Casitas to Kaw Gaming, Inc., a Native American tribe in Oklahoma, and just yesterday issued a press release saying that shipment of those orders began last week, with more shipping this week. If that short timeline from order to shipment indicates that it is shipping finished inventory, that would certainly be a positive sign for deliveries, cash flow, and inventory management.

Industry observers note that BOXABL’s July Nasdaq listing provided access to public equity markets but not the large infusion of unrestricted operating cash the firm likely hoped for. After shareholder redemptions, the business combination generated approximately $47.2 million in gross trust proceeds. About $31.1 million was allocated to obligations under an equity prepaid forward transaction, and additional closing costs reduced the net increase in unrestricted cash to approximately $6.5 million.

In a recent development, the firm established an at-the-market stock (ATM) offering program on September 25th, authorizing up to $100 million in equity sales. As of November 6, the company had generated about $646,000 in gross proceeds from the stock issuance. Notably, the program was initiated in late September, when the stock traded just under $4 per share.

The organization issued very little equity in the six weeks after initiating the program (when the stock was at a higher price, relative to the November 24th closing price of $0.95), but some of this likely reflects restrictions on issuance during the quiet period before reporting results for the quarter.

Industry observers note that management believes that existing cash, product sales, forward-transaction proceeds, and future equity sales can fund operations for the next 12 months. The company also reported approximately $2.7 million in additional forward-transaction receipts from October 1 to November 6. Given recent trends, it appears unlikely that the company will become cash flow positive from operations in the near term. In addition, with the stock now trading below $1 per share, issuing equity at this level would not generate significant capital and would send a worrisome signal about the company’s liquidity.

Industry observers note that those resources provide some financial flexibility, but the gap between authorization to raise capital and actually securing it remains significant. BOXABL can continue cutting costs, seek additional financing or strategic partners, focus on markets with more favorable delivery conditions, and prioritize converting finished inventory into revenue.

In a recent development, each alternative involves trade-offs. Cutting expenses preserves cash but can constrain efforts to accelerate deliveries. Slowing production reduces near-term spending but weakens overhead absorption. Raising equity extends the operating runway but may dilute existing shareholders. Narrowing the company’s product or geographic focus could improve execution while postponing the scale central to its original economic proposition.

Recent findings suggest that these are not necessarily signs of an inevitable endpoint. They are choices facing a capital-dependent manufacturer whose commercial progress has not yet matched the resources needed to sustain operations. The longer that gap persists, the more difficult it becomes to preserve every element of the company’s original ambitions.

It has been revealed that experienced homebuilding leaders approach industrialized construction ventures with both interest and skepticism, for good reason. They recognize the efficiency potential of factory production. They also know that housing profitability depends on capital allocation, customer demand, regulatory compliance, construction execution, and cash conversion.

Those disciplines become more demanding when borrowing costs remain elevated, input costs are under pressure, and homebuyers demand concessions to overcome affordability constraints.

BOXABL’s financial challenges do not invalidate industrialized construction. Different approaches to modular production, panelization, and off-site manufacturing entail distinct capital requirements and operating models.

Recent findings suggest that but its latest disclosures illustrate how difficult it can be to translate manufacturing innovation into a financially sustainable housing enterprise. The next several quarters will show whether BOXABL can accelerate deliveries, reduce inventory exposure, improve manufacturing margins, and secure sufficient liquidity without further constraining its flexibility.

The company has made some progress in slowing its cash outflow, and those improvements deserve recognition. It also continues to operate at a substantial loss, consuming considerably more cash than its products generate and depending on financial and operational improvements that remain uncertain.

According to recent reports, BOXABL’s challenge is no longer primarily to persuade investors and customers that industrialized housing could transform residential construction. It is to demonstrate, through completed deliveries, disciplined working-capital management, and eventually positive cash flow, that its approach can sustain a business.

Sources indicate that the firm’s recent hiring may indicate that it’s doing all it can to deliver on this. Since September 15th, the company has hired Larry King as Chief Financial Officer, Heather Clayton as Chief Accounting Officer, Josef Elimlich to oversee sales strategy and the structure and performance of the sales organization, and Antonio Gonzalez as director of home delivery. While the company likely should have had the right people in these roles some time ago, the hires may indicate that it recognizes its challenges and is working to resolve them.

In homebuilding, being built for difficult conditions means more than having a promising product or innovative manufacturing process. It means having an operating model that can produce, deliver, and earn its way forward when capital is expensive, buyers are cautious, and the market offers little forgiveness for execution problems.

It has been revealed that that’s a standard BOXABL, founded in 2017 and boasting having raised more than $230 million from more than 50,000 investors, now must meet. Otherwise, it will join scores of prior valiant, promising, deeply-funded ventures that got caught in the echo chamber of not-exactly-here and not-quite-yet.

Marlowe raises $277M to build inference clusters with chips from Nvidia rivals

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial intelligence infrastructure startup Marlowe AI Inc.
  • In a recent development, bessemer, Altimeter, Emergence Capital and a number of other institutional bakers chipped in as well.
  • In a recent development, marlowe was founded last year by CEO Dan Lewis and Chief Technology Officer Kutta Srinivasan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:49 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Artificial intelligence infrastructure startup Marlowe AI Inc. has closed a huge $227 million seed round led by Accel.

In a recent development, bessemer, Altimeter, Emergence Capital and a number of other institutional bakers chipped in as well. They were joined by a large group of angel investors that included the chief executives of Palo Alto Networks Inc, Uber Technologies Inc., Box Inc. and Dropbox Inc. GeekWire reported on Monday that Marlowe is valued at $1.15 billion.

In a recent development, marlowe was founded last year by CEO Dan Lewis and Chief Technology Officer Kutta Srinivasan. Lewis previously headed the Microsoft Corp. unit responsible for Copilot Studio, the tech giant’s AI agent development tool. Srinivasan was the techical lead of the manufacturer’s AI infrastructure group.

Marlowe is building AI data centers for inference workloads. The company will optimize each facility for a specific inference workload category by tailoring its chip mix, network configuration and software. Marlowe believes that its approach will provide better hardware efficiency than general-purpose graphics card clusters.

“Even modest gains in network architecture, power oversubscription, AI-driven fleet operations, and workload-specific inference optimization multiply to create a durable, 2-3x overall advantage in performance, availability, resiliency, and cost,” Lewis and Srinivasan wrote in Marlowe’s launch blog post.

Sources indicate that the organization plans to bring its first data center online  next month. It’s based on hardware from Etched Inc., an inference chip startup that was valued at $21 billion in August.

Graphics cards often use only a small fraction of their maximum clock speed to avoid overheating. Etched’s chip is less prone to overheating and can therefore operate at higher clock speeds, which boosts model performance. The company says that its accelerator provides “multiple times the FLOPs density” of graphics cards.

Etched ships its chips as part of custom-made inference racks. According to the organization, the systems feature an interconnect that can perform some data movement tasks more than four times faster than competing silicon. Etched’s rack design also includes custom power management and cooling components.

Marlowe’s second facility will come online in the second quarter of 2027. It will host racks based on Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s Helios design. A Helios rack hosts 72 AMD graphics cards along with central processing units and Pensando data processing units, or DPUs. The DPUs offload networking tasks from the other chips to leave more computing capacity for AI models.

Helios racks’ networking and power delivery links are arranged in a configuration that reduces the need for manual cable maintenance. Additionally, the coolant lines feature a so-called quick-disconnect design. They can be plugged and unplugged without the specialized tools usually needed for the task.

GeekWire reported that Marlowe has also signed a letter of intent for a third data center. According to the publication, each of the company’s planned facilities will provide tens of megawatts of computing capacity. One megawatt is enough to power several hundred homes.

Marlowe will use the proceeds from its seed round to finance hardware purchases and hire engineers.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin (BTC) bull and SkyBridge Capital founder Anthony Scaramucci has argued that the world's biggest cryptocurrency could find a critical bottom as soon as this week.

Scaramucci's comments follow the leading cryptocurrency's struggle to recover from a catastrophic crypto market crash that took BTC to its lowest price level in over two years.

In the latest episode of All Things Markets on Nov. 20, the SkyBridge Capital founder joined Galaxy Digital CEO Mike Novogratz to discuss a potential bottom for Bitcoin.

In a recent development, scaramucci shared his view that Bitcoin could see its bottom on Nov. 25, citing the cryptocurrency's four-year halving cycle as the driving force behind his comments.

"Before we came on, I asked ChatGPT when's the expected halving for Bitcoin," Scaramucci explained.

In a recent development, "And then when are we 500 days out from that halving? And the estimate was November 25th," he added.

This prediction stems from the idea that Bitcoin's price trends could follow a predictable four-year cycle that coincides with the cryptocurrency's halving events, when the fresh BTC supply is cut in half.

This theory suggests that Bitcoin could find its major bottom around the 500-day mark before its next halving, expected in 2028.

However, these theories are by no means a certainty when it comes to predicting future price action, especially with the current level of institutional participation and macroeconomic forces impacting the crypto market to an unprecedented extent.

During the conversation, Novogratz also took note of Bitcoin's history of forming double bottoms during its four-year cycles.

"And every four years, Bitcoin double bottomed," Novogratz remarked.

At the time, the Galaxy Digital CEO's comments suggested a potentially positive scenario, as Bitcoin had been able to hold its psychological $60,000 price level.

"If it doesn't break 60, that could be a good sign," he noted.

Sources indicate that unfortunately for Bitcoin, the cryptocurrency subsequently crashed below this critical price point. This has left some wondering whether the cryptocurrency has already found its ultimate bottom.

During the same conversation, Novogratz suggested that Bitcoin's short-term outlook could largely depend on the current situation in the stock market.

Specifically, the billionaire said that a rebound in tech stocks could lead to a strong rally in Bitcoin's price.

"If we put in a bottom in the next couple days in the S&P here, down 3% from here, down 5% from here. And we have a rally back up. Man, Bitcoin is going to rally hard with it," Novogratz predicted.

However, he also warned that Bitcoin could see a lot of market-driven movements going forward, as opposed to crypto-specific movements.

"I think we're going to be stuck tethered to general sentiment and risk," he remarked.

Novogratz also believes that Bitcoin could trade in a range between $60,000 and $75,000 before a breakout or breakdown becomes apparent.

Industry observers note that volkswagen revealed how much its latest ID. Cross will cost, with prices starting at around $35,000 in the UK. But if you’re hoping to get the cheaper version, you’ll have to wait a bit longer.

Sources indicate that after opening orders for the ID. Cross in Europe in July, Volkswagen is preparing to launch the entry-level electric SUV in the UK.

The ID. Cross is the all-electric equivalent of the T-Cross, Volkswagen’s smallest and most affordable SUV in Europe and the UK.

Recent findings suggest that following the ID. Polo, the ID. Cross is the latest from Volkswagen’s electric urban family of compact cars.

The electric SUV is 4,153 mm long, about the same length as the T-Cross, but its dedicated MEB+ platform offers more interior space. It seats five and offers a 475-liter boot, 20 liters more than the gas-powered T-Cross with the rear seats pushed all the way forward.

It has been revealed that when the rear seats are folded, the electric ID. Cross offers up to 1,345 liters of overall luggage volume.

Like in Europe, the Volkswagen ID. Cross will be available with two battery packs in the UK: a 37 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) pack and a 52 kWh nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) pack.

Recent findings suggest that the ID. Cross with the larger 52 kWh battery offers up to 265 miles of WLTP range, while the 37 kWh version provides up to 194 miles of WLTP range.

With DC fast charging of up to 105 and 88 kW, Volkswagen said the vehicle’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in as little as 23 minutes.

All versions are equipped with vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, allowing it to be used as a mobile power bank for an e-bike, campsite, or other external electronic devices.

Inside, the ID. Cross adopts VW’s revamped interior digital cockpit design. Cross adopts VW’s revamped interior digital cockpit design. The setup includes a 10.25″ Digital Cockpit Pro instrument display and a 12.9″ infotainment screen. Based on driver feedback, Volkswagen brought back physical buttons for climate control and other vehicle functions.

According to recent reports, volkswagen will open orders for the ID. Cross Life and Style trims in the UK with the 52 kWh battery and 208 hp (211 PS) motor will go on sale on Thursday, November 19, starting at £30,260 ($40,000) and £33,675 ($44,500), respectively.

The base ID. Cross Life and Style trims with the 37 kWh battery will go on sale in January 2027, with prices starting at £26,985 ($35,500) and £30,400 ($40,100).

Sources indicate that volkswagen stated the 52 kWh version is eligible for the UK government’s £1,500 ($2,000) electric car grant. Eligibility for the 37 kWh versions is expected to be confirmed soon.

In a recent development, in Europe, Volkswagen opened orders for the entry-level ID. Cross Trend last month, starting at €27,995 ($31,000) in Germany, including VAT.

Industry observers note that as the electric counterpart to its popular T-Cross, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer remarked the ID. Cross is “modern, reliable, and above all, affordable.”.

Sadly, VW has no plans to bring the ID. Cross to the US. In early 2027, it will launch the fresh ID. Tiguan, which will replace the outgoing ID.4 SUV.

Epochal launches with $100M to help developers train predictive AI models
