📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial intelligence tooling startup Epochal AI Inc.
  • Industry observers note that the capital was provided by Chief Executive Officer Guodong Zhang, a machine learning researcher who earlier co-founded xAI Corp.
  • Epochal’s first offering is a cloud service called the Epochal Time Portal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 20:30 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Artificial intelligence tooling startup Epochal AI Inc. released today with $100 million in funding.

Industry observers note that the capital was provided by Chief Executive Officer Guodong Zhang, a machine learning researcher who earlier co-founded xAI Corp. He established Epochal earlier this year with two other xAI co-founders, Zihang Dai and Manuel Kroiss. The manufacturer’s staff also includes former researchers from Anthropic PBC, OpenAI Group PBC and Google DeepMind.

Epochal’s first offering is a cloud service called the Epochal Time Portal. According to the organization, it enables developers to train AI models that can predict future events. The service does so by providing models with access to historical web data from the past 30 years.

Recent findings suggest that if a bank wishes to train an AI that can predict quarterly earnings, it could use the service to fetch financial results from the first three quarters of 2025. It could then ask the AI to estimate fourth-quarter results from the same year.

After the model generates its predictions, developers can compare them against real fourth-quarter earnings to check the model’s accuracy. They can make adjustments if necessary and then repeat the training workflow until the model starts generating accurate forecasts.

The Epochal Time Portal features more than 1 trillion historical web pages on launch. Each entry includes a timestamp that indicates when it was created. According to the manufacturer, its timestamps make it possible to track how a web page changed over time.

Industry observers note that AI models access the content through a purpose-built search engine. It enables them to specify the time periods from which they wish to retrieve web pages. According to Epochal, its platform provides one-minute granularity for the most frequently updated pages.

In a recent development, like consumer search engines, the Epochal Time Portal prioritizes the web pages that are most relevant to each given query. The difference is that it considers web pages’ creation date when evaluating relevance. If a query contains the term “Meta” but asks for pages created before 2021, the year Facebook Inc. rebranded, the Epochal Time Portal will not bring up pages that relate to the social networking giant.

Today’s frontier models can determine that they’re being trained on historical data rather than up-to-date information. For example, a model might compare the creation date of a web page to the virtual clock of the operating system on which it deployed. Such discrepancies can lower the effectiveness of training runs.

According to Epochal, its service mitigates the matter by deploying AI models in sandboxes synced to their training data. If a company is training a model on we pages from 2025, the Epochal Time Portal will run it on a Linux version from that year. It applies the same precautions to the software tools and programming language versions that models use.

The Epochal Time Portal is initially available in a single free tier with low usage limits. Epochal plans to follow up the launch by sharing the results of several AI experiments that its researchers have carried out using the service.

#134546. How real estate agents handle proof of funds and disclosures

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1181 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

How real estate agents handle proof of funds and disclosures

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1181 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On a recent coaching call this week, an agent asked a question that looks tactical and is actually about professional discipline.
  • Let me give the coaching first, because the sequence is where most agents go wrong.
  • Proof of funds gets requested too early and in the wrong tone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On a recent coaching call this week, an agent asked a question that looks tactical and is actually about professional discipline. She works mostly in commercial, she has a physician buying a home and several of her clients have investors behind them, which makes gathering proof of funds a real ordeal. When do I ask for it? Does it need to be current? And how do I protect something that private? Those questions sit squarely on the line between being a salesperson and being a fiduciary, and that line is where our industry keeps getting tested.

Let me give the coaching first, because the sequence is where most agents go wrong.

Proof of funds gets requested too early and in the wrong tone. Imagine a buyer who just called on an ad. If the first thing you do is hand them a list of documents, you have converted a warm first contact into homework, and you have done it before you have given them a single reason to trust you. I do not open any client relationship by burdening the person with tasks. The order has to serve the relationship, not the file.

Recent findings suggest that here is the sequence I teach. Get them into the office first. On that opening call you can ask one soft question, do you happen to have a proof of funds ready, and if the answer is no, you keep it light. We will need it at some point, bring it when we meet if you can, but do not worry about it now. You have raised the flag without turning it into a barrier.

When they arrive, run a genuine buyer appointment and get the buyer to hire you, the same way you would work to get hired by a seller. Only then do you assign the homework, and now the identical list that would have felt like a wall on the phone lands as a plan. Here is what we need from you, and in the meantime let’s define exactly what you are looking for, let me show you what is available, and we can even see a couple so you get a feel for the market. The serious looking begins once I have the documents. The buyer never feels interrogated. They feel represented.

Powerfact: You earn the right to ask for documents by first earning the relationship.

Now to the part that matters for leaders, because it is about how we protect our businesses and our clients at the same time.

She asked whether to send buyers to their own bank or recommend someone she knows. I prefer to recommend my own lender, and I say that carefully, because we are operating in a litigation environment, and the professional move is to assume you could be sued and to run your business so that you are covered. Practically, that means disclosing any financial relationship in writing, every time. On our coaching platform I built a document I call the Transparency Conversation, a simple editable form that states who you are connected to, how you get paid, and whether anyone shares in a fee. If the lender is tied to your company and a financial arrangement exists, that gets disclosed plainly. If you are recommending someone purely because you know and trust the loan officer, you say exactly that and nothing more.

Industry observers note that here is how I used to present the recommendation itself, and the logic has aged well. You can use any lender you want, that is your call. The reason I like my person is this. I could refer a lot of lenders, and I choose this one, because if he ever lets you down, he does not just lose your loan, he loses every piece of business I will ever send him. So he will do whatever it takes, within the rules, to get you to the closing table. That framing respects the buyer’s freedom and explains why your recommendation carries weight. It is service, stated out loud.

Industry observers note that her question was about confidentiality. She had a buyer with roughly $2 million in proof of funds, and people are private about money at that level. Does it become confidential? Do we keep the figure quiet even though we hold the documentation?

This is where the fiduciary line gets drawn. The moment a buyer hires you, they stop being a customer and become a client, and that shift carries a duty. Anything they share with you stays with you unless they authorize otherwise. So think like an attorney. When the information is this sensitive, you protect it with a document. Have the client sign an authorization that permits you to share their financial information only with the parties who truly need it to assemble the transaction. You can adapt the Transparency Conversation form for exactly this. Now you can do your job, the client’s privacy is respected, and you have a record that protects both of you.

According to recent reports, another agent said she never provides proof of funds until after an offer is accepted. That is a sound default in many cases, but it depends on the seller. On luxury homes, estates, and commercial property, the listing side will often require proof of funds before they open the door, and that is legitimate. Sellers of a multimillion dollar property do not want a stream of non-buyers touring for decorating ideas or dream-board photos. When you represent that buyer, prepare them for the requirement so a reasonable request does not feel like an insult.

For brokers and team leaders, here is the translation. Our industry has spent two years being told that our compensation and our value must be disclosed, documented, and justified. Good. The agents who will thrive under that scrutiny are the ones who already behave like fiduciaries by habit, not the ones who treat disclosure as a form to dodge. Teach your people the sequence, relationship first, documents second. Standardize the written disclosures so no agent is improvising a legal boundary on the fly. And model the confidentiality, because a buyer who sees you guard their two million dollar statement like it is your own will refer you for the rest of their life.

Recent findings suggest that the whole thing fits on one page. Do not lead with the paperwork. Get them in, get them to hire you, assign the homework as part of the service. Recommend your lender, and disclose everything in writing. Treat their financial information as a fiduciary, with a signed authorization. And read the other side of the transaction, so you know when a request for proof is simply professionalism doing its job.

Make it 8: Connecticut joins first responder homebuying push

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Connecticut is the latest state to help first responders reach their homeownership goals with assistance for down payments and closing costs.
  • The “First Responders’ Time to Own” program gives state and local police officers, full-time and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical service personnel $25,000 in forgivable assistance through the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority (CHFA) and the Connecticut Department of Housing.
  • In addition to down payment and closing cost help, the program gives applicants a 0.125 percentage point interest rate reduction on their CHFA first mortgage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Connecticut is the latest state to help first responders reach their homeownership goals with assistance for down payments and closing costs.

The “First Responders’ Time to Own” program gives state and local police officers, full-time and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical service personnel $25,000 in forgivable assistance through the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority (CHFA) and the Connecticut Department of Housing. To qualify, first responders must have completed two years of service and purchase a primary residence within the community they serve.

In addition to down payment and closing cost help, the program gives applicants a 0.125 percentage point interest rate reduction on their CHFA first mortgage.

“Connecticut’s police officers, firefighters and EMS personnel dedicate themselves to protecting our families and communities, and we want to make sure they have the opportunity to build their own futures here,” Governor Ned Lamont stated in a prepared statement on Tuesday. “By helping reduce one of the biggest barriers to buying a home, we’re investing in the people who serve our state and the communities that depend on them.”.

The program is part of Public Act 26-12, a state bill that aims to increase the number of first responders with a number of incentives, including college tuition reimbursement and improved labor protections.

“The people who protect and serve our communities should be able to afford to live in those communities, and this program with help them do it,” Comptroller Sean Scanlon said in a written statement. “Helping the people who put their lives on the line for us every day buy their first home is literally the least we can do, and I’m proud to have worked with Governor Lamont and legislature to make this a reality.”.

Sources indicate that seven other states also have down payment assistance programs for first responders. Florida, Nevada, Georgia and South Carolina provide flat amounts, ranging from $10,000 to $35,000. Texas, Maryland and Ohio’s programs are percentage-based and offer assistance ranging from 2.5 percent to 5 percent of the purchase price.

The terms of each program vary. Most states forgive the assistance after five to seven years, but Nevada requires homebuyers to repay the funds within 30 years. And like Connecticut, Ohio also offers a 0.25 percent mortgage rate discount.

According to recent reports, “Homeownership offers more than a place to live. It creates stability, strengthens connections to community and provides an opportunity to build wealth over time,” CHFA CEO and Executive Director Nandini Natarajan said in an announcement. “Through First Responders’ Time to Own, we’re helping the people who answer the call for our communities take an important step toward achieving their own homeownership goals.”.

First responders often fall through the cracks of housing assistance programs because they don’t earn enough to afford market-rate housing but earn too much to qualify for federal housing vouchers.

It has been revealed that inman explored this dilemma last September in a feature on workforce housing in resort towns like Jackson Hole, Vail and Tahoe. These towns can’t operate without first responders and other essential workers in the hospitality and retail sectors. However, rental and for-sale home prices have far outpaced what these workers earn, forcing them to commute long distances from more affordable towns or take on second and third jobs to survive.

The solution for some of these towns has been investing in workforce housing, which caps prices for households that earn between 60 percent and 120 percent of their area’s AMI. Most workforce housing is rent-only, but some states are extending the programs to include for-sale properties.

“I think the fact that workforce housing can be necessary or is a thing in the first place is really an indictment of the state of housing affordability in the country today,” Realtor.com Senior Economist Jake Krimmel remarked. “I think it’s crucial to ground any conversation about workforce and affordable housing in that reality. It’s a market failure and a policy failure that someone could be a doctor, a teacher or another kind of professional and cannot afford to pay the market rent or own a home outright.”.

Windermere Principal Economist Jeff Tucker noted workforce housing isn’t a panacea for affordability and works within an ecosystem of other housing and economic policies, such as upzoning, to create a more equitable market.

Recent findings suggest that tucker’s comments came a month after the Senate introduced the ROAD to Housing Act of 2025, and three months before the House introduced the Housing for the 21st Century Act. The bills were eventually combined into the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which passed in June.

It has been revealed that “A broad package of necessary reforms to make more housing construction possible in much of the country is a really important component of a long-term solution to the housing affordability challenges we face,” Tucker remarked. “Our current housing shortage took years to develop. So it’ll take years to build our way out of it.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 20:41 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Employees working at frontier artificial intelligence model companies Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC have been butting heads with executives over advanced models whose reasoning is such that the models pose to danger to humanity, according to a report by Axios today based on more than two dozen sources familiar with the current standoff at the companies.

The report states the models in question are far more powerful than anything that has so far reached the public, showing great leaps forward in reasoning in many areas that have been difficult, “if not impossible,” to control during tests. It appears that some staff err on the side of caution and believe the training should stop completely while others believe they can be reined in.

According to recent reports, “If we continue trying to make models much smarter, such that they’re actually smarter than us… they will in fact be able to trick us successfully,” one of the researchers told Axios. “And once you get to that point, many of the schemes that we’ve had at work up until now sort of go out the window.”.

After Open AI’s AI agents seemingly went berserk earlier this year and hacked the open-source AI platform Hugging Face Inc., there have been calls to pause AI development until safety can be assured. The state of California this month launched a lawsuit calling Open AI a “public nuisance,” whose models currently pose cybersecurity risks while threatening the “well-being of society.”.

According to recent reports, the debate on how far we should go before we step on the brakes has largely been overshadowed by companies, and the countries where they are developed, steaming ahead winning the AI race. In the Axios report, many of the anonymous claimed executives are “out of touch” with safety challenges as they put profit first.

In a recent development, nonetheless, Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei has been vocal about the “existential risks to humanity” that AI might bring. In his recent essay, “We Must Pace the Frontier,” Amodei remarked “pacing” is vital, warning that authoritarian regimes such as China must agree to cooperate in moving forward slowly with the frontier models. President Trump has been less than supportive of such measures, calling the threats to humanity a “hoax.”.

Luminate Bank buys Real Genius mortgage unit

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Minneapolis-based Luminate Bank has agreed to acquire select assets and the mortgage origination operations of Real Genius, expanding the bank’s reach into the digital mortgage channel, the companies announced Wednesday.
  • Sources indicate that online consumer-direct lender Real Genius, which was originally a division of FirstBank, will operate as a division of Luminate Bank and remain as a consumer-facing brand.
  • Nathan Raich, executive vice president of mortgage lending at Luminate Bank, noted the move is aimed at giving borrowers more flexibility in how they work with the institution.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Minneapolis-based Luminate Bank has agreed to acquire select assets and the mortgage origination operations of Real Genius, expanding the bank’s reach into the digital mortgage channel, the companies announced Wednesday.

Sources indicate that online consumer-direct lender Real Genius, which was originally a division of FirstBank, will operate as a division of Luminate Bank and remain as a consumer-facing brand. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Nathan Raich, executive vice president of mortgage lending at Luminate Bank, noted the move is aimed at giving borrowers more flexibility in how they work with the institution.

“Some homebuyers want a mortgage professional beside them at every step, while others prefer a more self-directed, digital experience,” Raich noted in a statement. “Mortgage lending isn’t becoming exclusively digital or exclusively relationship-driven. The opportunity is to be great at both and give customers the freedom to choose.”.

Luminate Bank was formed after a team of mortgage executives acquired the bank in 2020, with a strategy of building a “concierge” financial experience that blends traditional mortgage lending with depository services, co-founder and president of mortgage lending Eric Lovins noted in a recent interview with HousingWire’s Reverse Mortgage Daily.On the Real Genius deal, Lovins said that Luminate has been working on integration planning and evaluating the organizational structure.

“Our focus is on creating a strong platform for sustainable, profitable growth while ensuring we have the right people, resources and infrastructure to support the business,” he remarked.

According to Lovins, Real Genius’s leadership team previously helped build and operate FirstBank’s ConsumerDirect mortgage platform, which delivered more than 50,000 loans over nine years and contributed to a mortgage business that generated approximately $6 billion in annual production. In 2012, the division of FirstBank became Real Genius under the leadership of CEO Jamie Thornton.

“We see tremendous value in that experience and the opportunity to build on it,” Lovins said.

According to recent reports, he added that the deal leverages Luminate’s broader mortgage and banking platform and represents another vital step in expanding its national mortgage presence. The manufacturer’s strategy continues to focus on both organic growth and strategic acquisitions.

According to recent reports, earlier this year, Luminate acquired assets of Illinois-based First State Mortgage Services, extending its footprint across the Midwest and central U.S. Many members of First State Mortgage’s team, led by CEO and president Rene Shaffer, joined Luminate.

Luminate has originated about $3.8 billion year to date, according to mortgage technology platform InGenius. The organization had 433 sponsored loan officers as of Wednesday, per the Nationwide Multistate Licensing System.

It has been revealed that in December 2022, Luminate Home Loans — a subsidiary of the bank that has operated since 1998 — brought the more than 200-member NEO Home Loans team, previously part of Celebrity Home Loans, onto its platform. This boosted Luminate’s distributed retail presence at a time when many independent mortgage banks were contracting.

In October 2024, however, Luminate revealed that it would shut down the NEO Home Loans division. The firm noted the decision was driven by a desire to “focus on integrating mortgage lending into its core banking services to better serve clients and build long-term financial relationships.” The NEO group is now partnered with AI-focused mortgage lender Better.com.

UPDATED 20:54 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Rajiv Ramaswami is stepping down from his role as chief executive of Nutanix Inc., six years after he joined the hyperconverged cloud infrastructure firm from its rival VMware Inc.

In a letter to organization employees, Ramaswami (pictured) stated he’s going to continue in the role for the time being while he works with Nutanix’s board of directors to identify a successor and assist with the transition. “After that, I will continue to serve as a senior advisor to the company for a period of time,” he said in the letter.

Ramaswami, who is 60 years old, did not give any reason for his coming departure, but the letter seems to indicate that he’s not ready to retire just yet.

“Our next CEO will inherit a strong platform, a loyal customer base and, most importantly, an exceptional team,” Ramaswami wrote. “Until then, my focus remains on leading this company and nothing about our day-to-day priorities changes. I am committed to helping our next leader succeed, and my ask of you, as always, is to continue to focus on executing as we go through this leadership transition.”.

Ramaswami added that Nutanix has hired an executive search firm to lead the hunt for his successor. The news came as the organization delivered its first-quarter earnings report, posting modest year-over-year gains in profit and revenue.

Industry observers note that the manufacturer reported adjusted earnings of 73 cents per share, beating Wall Street’s target of 61 cents per share by a strong margin. Revenue for the period came to $772.4 million, up 15% from a year earlier and above the Street’s forecast of $762.7 million.

Industry observers note that nutanix’s outlook for the current quarter is strong, with the company guiding for sales of between $820 million and $830 million, compared with the Street’s consensus estimate of $820.4 million. However, the full-year picture is a little less rosy, with Nutanix guiding for annual sales of $3.18 billion to $3.23 billion. The midpoint of that range trails the Street’s forecast of $3.22 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue.

Investors did not take the news very well. The cautious full-year guidance compared with the uncertainty over leadership prompted many to sell, and Nutanix’s stock was down 8% after-hours, having already fallen more than 5% during the regular trading session, on a down day for many tech stocks.

Virginia Gambale, of the board at Nutanix, hailed the “tremendous impact” Ramaswami had on the tech giant during his six-year tenure. “Rajiv led the company’s transformation to subscription software, built a loyal and expanding global enterprise base and established a technology portfolio that we believe positions us well for the AI era,” she mentioned. “We’re focused on selecting an exceptional leader who can build on that foundation.”.

In a conference call with analysts, Ramaswami noted he believes the company is embarking on the third major chapter in its history. The first chapter, before his arrival, saw the company establish itself as the leader of the hyperconverged infrastructure industry. Chapter two began when he took over, and saw Nutanix expand from those roots to become a platform company, he said.

Sources indicate that “[We have] transformed the manufacturer to be profitable while growing and expanding the product portfolio quite significantly, from HCI to a platform that works across clouds, supports external storage and has cloud-native capabilities and now moving into the future with AI capabilities,” Ramaswami said. “Chapter two is well-established at this point and there’s a lot of opportunity in terms of driving growth. I feel like we are in a very good place.”.

Recent findings suggest that according to Ramaswami, Nutanix now stands at an inflection point as it looks to cash in on the new era of artificial intelligence. “I’ve been talking to the board for a bit about this, as well as in terms of our strategic direction and the timing for succession, and so we came to the conclusion together that this is perhaps the right time,” he told analysts. “[We wanted] to announce it ahead of time as we look for the appropriate next leader.”.

According to recent reports, ramaswami’s departure from the firm should at least be a lot smoother than his arrival. Nutanix announced it had appointed Ramaswami as its CEO in late 2020, just two days after he quit his role as chief operating officer of its biggest rival, VMware.

VMware was indignant about the manner of his departure, and responded with a lawsuit that accused Ramaswami of breaching his legal and contractual duties to the company by “secretly meeting” with Nutanix’s board to discuss taking over, while continuing to play a leading role in shaping its product and business strategy. The lawsuit was ultimately settled out of court about a year later.

  • Industry observers note that ethereum developers want to change the gas accounting for validator deposits.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Industry observers note that ethereum developers want to change the gas accounting for validator deposits. The plan is to measure the request bytes that these deposit events create.

In a recent development, the gas calculation already accounts for executing a deposit. However, after the deposit is finished, a 192-byte request is passed along with the block. Those 192 bytes are excluded from the minimum gas charge, so the same gas limit might allow more data than the initial calculation accounts for.

Sources indicate that under Gloas, there is no fixed cap on the number of deposit requests per block. The execution layer has not capped this either. Gas is the only limiting factor.

Industry observers note that neither EIP-8131 nor EIP-8279 accounts for those request bytes. This means that deposits could become another way to bypass the gas floor once EIP-8279 closes the loophole involving cold storage reads.

In a recent development, A relay contract can call the deposit contract repeatedly, costing around 26,000 gas per deposit. In the author's example, that execution cost is below the point where the gas floor for zero-byte calldata would start to increase the total charge.

This results in a payload of about 1.44 times the block gas limit divided by 64, compared with about 1.15 times the same baseline.

The main issue is the data size, so the proposal directly addresses the data.

A log from the deposit contract with the deposit event topic counts as 192 bytes before the log entry is added. This is the same condition EIP-6110 uses to turn logs into requests.

The cost of this would be another check that client developers would have to implement and test.

Users are not expected to pay more for regular deposits. The cost of executing a regular deposit is already above the proposed minimum, so the extra 12,288 gas only raises the minimum charge.

The proposal has yet to be scheduled for a network upgrade.

#134534. Tesla on Autopilot/FSD hit an overturned truck at 71 mph, killing 3

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1483 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla on Autopilot/FSD hit an overturned truck at 71 mph, killing 3

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1483 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Tesla Model 3 drove into an overturned box truck on I-75 near Naples, Florida, killing two of its passengers and a man who had stopped to help.
  • Sources indicate that police and local media covered the May 31 crash as a truck wreck in the dark, and none of it mentioned a driver-assist system.
  • on Sunday, May 31, 2026, the 31-year-old driver of a 2014 Freightliner lost the road near the Pine Ridge Road exit in Collier County, steered back onto southbound I-75, and flipped it, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Tesla Model 3 drove into an overturned box truck on I-75 near Naples, Florida, killing two of its passengers and a man who had stopped to help. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators claims Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, at 71 mph.

Sources indicate that police and local media covered the May 31 crash as a truck wreck in the dark, and none of it mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data, and it lands as Tesla’s monthly crash count hits another record.

Just before 4 a.m. on Sunday, May 31, 2026, the 31-year-old driver of a 2014 Freightliner lost the road near the Pine Ridge Road exit in Collier County, steered back onto southbound I-75, and flipped it, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The overturned truck ended up blocking the center and outside lanes.

Jonathan Garcia Arias, a 25-year-old Naples man and former Marine, was driving by in a BMW. He pulled over and got out to help the truck driver.

Then a southbound 2023 Tesla with five young men from Naples inside came up on the scene. FHP’s report notes the front of the Tesla hit the underside of the overturned truck and Garcia Arias. Two of the Tesla’s passengers, aged 18 and 19, died at the scene, and Garcia Arias died later in the hospital. The 20-year-old driver and two more passengers were seriously hurt.

A few days later, FHP used the crash as a warning about stopping near wrecks on the interstate. Senior Trooper Kenn Watson stated the Tesla driver would have seen only the truck’s underside, with “no lights, no reflectors, nothing warning them.”.

Sources indicate that so that’s the official story. A dark obstacle, a driver who couldn’t see it in time. Nobody mentioned a word about Autopilot.

Under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone was killed or hurt. Tesla filed one for this crash.

In a recent development, it identifies the car as a 2023 Model 3 on a highway, flags a traffic incident on the roadway, and marks the automation “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That means Tesla confirmed through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 71 mph and a fatality, lists the Florida Highway Patrol as the investigating agency, and notes it learned of the crash from police and the media.

Then it blacks out the crash narrative, the software version, and whether the road was within the system’s approved operating domain, all as “confidential business information.” That’s the same redaction Tesla applies to 99.9% of its reports.

The report also surfaced late. Tesla filed it as a 5-Day report, the urgent category for fatal crashes, but it didn’t land until Tesla’s September filings, more than three months after the crash. And Tesla lists law enforcement as one of the ways it found out about it.

In a recent development, how we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 07:56 UTC, which converts to 3:56 a.m. in Florida, two minutes off the 3:54 a.m. in FHP’s report. The city, the highway, the 2023 model year, the month and the fatal outcome all line up, and it’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report in Naples that month. It’s the same crash.

In a recent development, A Tesla on driver-assist going highway speed into the underside of a big truck, in the dark, in Florida. If that sounds familiar, it should.

In 2016, Joshua Brown was killed near Williston when his Model S on Autopilot drove under a tractor-trailer crossing the highway. In 2019, Jeremy Banner died in Delray Beach when his Model 3 on Autopilot went under a trailer at 68 mph and had its roof sheared off. In both crashes, neither the driver nor the system braked.

In a recent development, trooper Watson’s point was that a human couldn’t see the truck. But a major, unlit obstacle sitting across two lanes at night is exactly the kind of thing a driver-assist system is supposed to catch, and Tesla now sells FSD as nearly ready to drive with nobody watching. And an attentive driver could clearly see it, as the BMW driver did, and stop before the Tesla arrived.

Sources indicate that we want to be fair about what the data doesn’t prove. “Engaged within 30 seconds” is the reporting trigger. Tesla’s 71 mph may be a telematics snapshot rather than the impact speed. And with the software version redacted, we can’t say whether this was Autopilot or FSD.

Recent findings suggest that the NHTSA release that surfaced this crash, covering filings through October 15, also set a new monthly high. Tesla reported 264 driver-assist crashes in September 2026, beating July’s 236, which was itself a record. That’s up from 135 in March.

Sources indicate that september may still grow as late reports come in. This Naples crash highlights how late they can be.

Recent findings suggest that our merged dataset now holds 4,669 Tesla driver-assist crash reports since 2019, 69 of them flagged fatal. The same release added two other fatal reports, both “Verified Engaged” and both covered locally with no mention of driver-assist: a Model Y that hit a tree and burned in El Dorado Hills, California, killing three, and a Model X that hit a signal pole in Naples on September 30, killing a passenger. We’ll lay those out separately.

Three people died on I-75, including a man who got out of his car to help a stranger. Tesla knows its driver-assist was on, knows the speed, holds the telematics, and filed a federal report saying so. Then it sealed everything that would explain what the car did, and the public got a story about a dark truck.

That's what happens when the system has to identify all objects in the camera frame before it can start to estimate the objects position and then relative distance and then relative velocity. Unrecognizable objects will destroy all your logic. This is a design failure and not something Tesla can actually fix.

Recent findings suggest that compare that to radars and lidars that directly measure distances and relative velocities of everything in front of the car, regardless of what it is. That is a far better approach because you do not want the car the impact objects on its trajectory regardless of what those objects turn out to be.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recognized for contributions to the design and development of automotive electrification systems, one of the highest honors in U.S.
  • Tomy Sebastian of HL Mechatronics, HL Mando's North American R&D hub for intelligent mobility technologies, has been elected to the U.S.
  • Sources indicate that election to the NAE is considered one of the highest honors in the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recognized for contributions to the design and development of automotive electrification systems, one of the highest honors in U.S. engineering.

AUBURN, Mich., Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dr. Tomy Sebastian of HL Mechatronics, HL Mando's North American R&D hub for intelligent mobility technologies, has been elected to the U.S. National Academy of Engineering (NAE) as a member of its 2026 class. His election recognizes his contributions to the design and development of automotive electrification systems.

Sources indicate that election to the NAE is considered one of the highest honors in the U.S. engineering community. Members are selected based on the significance and impact of their engineering achievements, with a limited number elected each year. A founding member of HL Mechatronics, Dr. Sebastian has led advances in automotive motor and control technologies. One of his major achievements was the application of permanent-magnet motors to electric power steering (EPS) systems. By addressing vibration and noise caused by torque ripple, and reducing costs, his work helped lay the foundation for wider adoption of the technology. His expertise has also been recognized by the international engineering community. In 2003, he was elected a Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), a distinction held by no more than 0.1 percent of IEEE members and awarded in recognition of exceptional technical achievements. He served as president of the IEEE Industry Applications Society (IAS) from 2017 to 2018 and received the IEEE Nikola Tesla Award in 2019 for his achievements in the fields of power electronics and motors. Over several decades, Dr. Sebastian has contributed to the advancement of automotive motor technology. He has published more than 60 technical papers and holds approximately 30 U.S. patents.

Meanwhile, Dr. Mohammad Islam, Chief Scientist at HL Mechatronics, has received the IEEE IAS Gerald Kliman Innovator Award. Dr. Islam has helped drive a paradigm shift in steering systems by designing motors essential to the electrification of hydraulic steering systems. The motor and sensor technologies he developed are now used in tens of millions of vehicles worldwide.

Recent findings suggest that commenting on the achievements, the two engineers said, "We are deeply honored by these meaningful achievements. They would not have been possible without the outstanding colleagues we worked with." They added, "We will continue to pursue advanced technology development with an unwavering spirit of inquiry and contribute to strengthening HL Mechatronics' competitiveness.".

HL Mechatronics is HL Mando's research hub for intelligent mobility technologies. Established in 2013 in Detroit, a center of the North American automotive industry, the manufacturer designs future motion technologies by integrating hardware and software. It has integrated engineering capabilities spanning electrical, mechanical and control engineering, as well as system safety and validation, supported by core technologies including electronic systems, embedded software, motors and sensors. Building on its expertise in mobility, HL Mechatronics is advancing next-generation precision motion control technologies and expanding into newly introduced industries and markets.

SOURCE HL Mechatronics; HL Mando; HL Group.

The agreement, confirmed Tuesday in the tech giant’s Week 7 Better 2.0 scorecard, is expected to provide a lower-cost customer acquisition channel.

The tech giant has received five term sheets for about $50 million in debt financing tied to the proposed sale of the bank and is continuing discussions with prospective financing partners.

The company said its AI-powered HELOC partnership with a large existing customer is live, with volume increasing weekly. Better is also preparing a multichannel campaign to expand the product through its wholesale platform and onboard additional brokerages.

Sources indicate that four more mortgage brokerages are in the pipeline to join the platform. Two previously declared partnerships — with a rental credit management platform and a home inspection company — are expected to launch early next week.

Latest Update: Anthropic is trying to kill traditional desktop apps with Claude-generated desktop apps

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that rarely a day goes by that Anthropic PBC doesn’t announce some kind of new capability, feature or model, and today wasn’t any different.
  • It promises to be one of its more impactful updates, fanning the flames of those who argue that artificial intelligence is ultimately destined to eat the software world.
  • The company said today that customers can now transform what it calls “artifacts” into standalone applications that run independently of Claude and can be accessed from the desktop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 21:36 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Industry observers note that rarely a day goes by that Anthropic PBC doesn’t announce some kind of new capability, feature or model, and today wasn’t any different. Today came the ability to use Claude to create fully functional desktop applications for Windows and Mac computers with a single prompt.

It promises to be one of its more impactful updates, fanning the flames of those who argue that artificial intelligence is ultimately destined to eat the software world.

The company said today that customers can now transform what it calls “artifacts” into standalone applications that run independently of Claude and can be accessed from the desktop. Artifacts have been around for a while, and they can be almost anything, such as a simple order tracker or a meeting dashboard that pulls information from the user’s calendar and email inbox.

Recent findings suggest that however, until today, artifacts were a bit tricky to access. They could be opened up only from inside Claude itself, which meant people first had to open up the chatbot, login and then find the old conversation where they originally created the artifact they want to use.

Industry observers note that anthropic remarked people are using Claude artifacts all the time for various everyday tasks, and so it makes sense to mature the concept. “If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention,” the manufacturer said.

That’s why Anthropic is making it possible for people to use artifacts to create, run and share desktop applications with Claude’s newly introduced “Install as App” feature, which is available in beta now on Windows and macOS.

Industry observers note that in a video posted on X, Anthropic demonstrated how straightforward it is to create a functional desktop app from a simple prompt. The user simply describes the tool they want Claude to create, click confirm and then sit back and wait for a few seconds as it slaps together the required code to bring that app to life.

You can now install Claude artifacts as desktop apps on Mac and Windows.

Ask Claude to build an artifact, click "Install as app", and open it like any other app. It can use your connectors and, if you allow it, send notifications or add a menu bar item. pic.twitter.com/8CBgqe5OKq.

— ClaudeDevs (@ClaudeDevs) November 24, 2026.

In a recent development, because these are “real” apps, they come with their own app icons and they open in a dedicated Window, rather than running within the Claude interface. They also get the ability to send notifications to people, Anthropic noted.

In a recent development, as an added benefit, Claude artifacts that are transformed into desktop apps will be able to use Claude and various third-party connectors, meaning that AI agents will be able to interact with them autonomously, Anthropic mentioned. However, the firm did warn that any requests made by an app to Claude will count toward their monthly credit usage, which means it could become expensive if an app is used excessively.

In a blog post Anthropic showcased a number of examples of what its internal teams have built, including a fully featured image editing app called Linnet, a file manager with a cinematic design called Phosphor, and a terminal application that integrates with Claude, which is known as Tern.

There is one major caveat to Claude artifacts-as-apps that sets them apart from traditional desktop applications. According to Anthropic, “you need to be online and signed in to Claude to open an app.”.

Recent findings suggest that that could be a pretty big downside, for many desktop applications are designed to work even if the computer is not connected to the internet. But those who lack a Wi-Fi connection will be unable to access their Claude-generated apps, even if they’re already built and configured.

#134530. What music sells a house? Agents say it’s not about genre

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1529 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

What music sells a house? Agents say it’s not about genre

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1529 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that taylor Swift, classical or silence?
  • Ask real estate agents what soundtrack sells a house, and you’ll get two answers.
  • Inman asked agents and brokers from Manhattan to Breckenridge, Colorado, and they described the music they play at showings and open houses and how they match it to the property.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that taylor Swift, classical or silence? Agents explain how they pick open house music, the one rule most follow and why none can prove it works.

Ask real estate agents what soundtrack sells a house, and you’ll get two answers. One is a carefully curated playlist, while the other is silence.

Inman asked agents and brokers from Manhattan to Breckenridge, Colorado, and they described the music they play at showings and open houses and how they match it to the property.

None could point to hard numbers showing a playlist moved a home faster or for more money. What they did offer was a clear set of rules from the agents who use music, and an equally firm argument from those who won’t touch it.

Sources indicate that ben Jacobs, co-founder of the Chestler Jacobs Team at Douglas Elliman in New York City, thinks music raises more questions than it answers. He mentioned he’s not a fan of playing music during showings.

In a recent development, “Buyers may wonder if the agent is trying to mask something, whether it’s street noise, construction nearby, sounds within the building or even a noisy appliance,” Jacobs told Inman. “You want buyers to experience the home as it actually is, without anything distracting from their ability to evaluate the space.”.

His co-founder, Jessica Chestler, noted music has its place. That place is just not a private showing.

“Music can be wonderful for setting a mood at a cocktail party, listing launch or special event, but during a showing, I think there’s something to be mentioned for letting the property speak for itself,” Chestler said.

According to recent reports, megan Sullivan works at the same brokerage, and she uses music for the very reason Jacobs avoids it. Sullivan sells large estate homes across Fairfield and Westchester counties out of Douglas Elliman’s Greenwich, Connecticut, office. Some of those homes sit within earshot of things a seller can’t fix.

Industry observers note that “I actually do like incorporating music into certain showings, particularly when a property is impacted by outside noise from planes, trains or automobiles,” Sullivan remarked. “Thoughtfully selected background music can help create a more welcoming atmosphere and soften those distractions, allowing buyers to focus on the overall experience of the home. I think it’s very property-specific.”.

Jeffrey Hensel is a broker associate with North Coast Financial, a California hard money lender that funds fix-and-flip and probate deals. He looks at it from the investor side.

It has been revealed that “Dead silence can amplify every creak, clank, and drip in an otherwise quiet home,” he said. “Background music masks these sounds and provides some white noise to help set a calm mood.”.

It has been revealed that agents in the pro-music camp mostly aren’t trying to cover anything up. They simply want buyers to stay longer.

Sandra Daniels of Harry Norman, Realtors | Forbes Global Properties serves the East Cobb and Marietta area outside Atlanta. She’s presently listing a $3.9 million estate in The River Club in Suwanee, Georgia.

For those showings, she rotates light classical piano, The Macarons Project and a Spotify playlist called “Nora Ephron + Nancy Meyers Dinner Party.”.

“Put a buyer in a home with a glass of Champagne or a cup of coffee and the right music playing, and that cozy, inviting atmosphere encourages people to stay, relax and feel at home,” Daniels told Inman.

Sources indicate that daniels also has a low-tech trick for vacant listings she expects to sell in the first week. She bought an old-school CD player and a few classical CDs. She leaves it on repeat through the first weekend of showings and stops by each evening to turn off the lights and music and lock up.

Natalia Bassova, founder and CEO of Resort Real Estate in Breckenridge, Colorado, saw the same effect at a luxury mountain listing. The home looked great, she said, but it revealed cold.

“By adding some background instrumental music, it gave the buyers more time to spend in the home. They spent more time in the kitchen and great room areas,” Bassova noted. “The property didn’t change, but the atmosphere did.”.

According to recent reports, for mountain and luxury homes, Bassova plays acoustic and piano music, including Ludovico Einaudi and The Piano Guys. For condos and new construction, she switches to soft contemporary instrumentals.

Agents who play music disagree on genre, but almost all agree on one thing: avoid lyrics.

“If the buyer begins to think about the music, then it is having a negative impact,” Bassova said. Her never-play list covers anything with strong lyrics, politics, swearing or heavy bass.

According to recent reports, andrea Seeney is a global real estate advisor with Atlanta Fine Homes Sotheby’s International Realty and a trained opera singer and classical pianist. She compared lyrics to a seller’s personal effects.

“Acoustic performances are best because they set a tone and allow the buyer to fill in the blanks with their own thoughts,” Seeney said.

It has been revealed that she leans toward jazz and usually plays Spotify’s Coffee House radio or its Ella Fitzgerald playlist. She states music works on buyers through memory: a song can take someone back to a time and place they enjoyed, “and that memory then reflects positively on the home.”.

It has been revealed that hensel takes the lyrics rule a step further, to genre itself. If an agent plays hip-hop or country for a buyer who doesn’t listen to it, he claims, that signals an assumption about who the buyer is. That can create friction neither side notices. His pick is quiet cocktail-lounge jazz like Miles Davis or Bill Evans, at a steady tempo and volume.

He also cited retail research by psychological scientists Adrian North and Lorraine Sheridan of Curtin University and Charles Areni of Macquarie University. It found that shoppers who heard classical music rated merchandise as higher quality and were willing to spend more.

Some agents ignore the rulebook completely.

Recent findings suggest that rachel Kilmer, an agent with ReeceNichols Real Estate in Kansas City, Missouri, plays Taylor Swift at nearly every open house. She swaps in country for more rural listings.

According to recent reports, “In Kansas City, she’s a conversation starter,” Kilmer stated. “People come in, and it’s, ‘Are you a Swiftie?’ ‘No, but I love the Chiefs!’ It really helps loosen up the conversation.”.

She added, “I’m the one sitting there listening to it for two hours!”.

Monica Shea, a broker with KW Aspire in Colorado Springs, Colorado, builds whole open houses around a theme, and the music follows.

According to recent reports, she played the Eras Tour set list at a Taylor Swift–themed open house and the Frozen soundtrack at a hot cocoa bar event. A Halloween open house got not-too-spooky Halloween music. For regular showings, she has sellers put on a YouTube channel with seasonal background music and scenery.

According to recent reports, shea’s never-play list puts her directly at odds with a few other agents: smooth jazz. Shea indicates she never plays “anything that sounds like the Weather Channel.”.

According to recent reports, marcel Finkelstein of Team BlackStar at eXp Realty hosts open houses every Sunday across Monmouth County, Newly introduced Jersey. He sees music as more of an icebreaker than a staging tool.

His Apple Music rotation includes lounge instrumentals, vocal-free dance-pop and Bon Entendeur. It also has Afro house from DJ Alex Niyazov and the warm trumpet and sax of Fausto Papetti and Paul Mauriat.

He uses the same approach whether the listing is a $600,000 two-bedroom condo in Manalapan or a $2 million six-bedroom in Colts Neck.

“I want the atmosphere to feel calm, comfortable and welcoming, rather than like a sales presentation,” Finkelstein said.

Finkelstein added that his Instagram followers also know how much he loves music.

“Every week, I share fresh songs and incorporate music into my stories and posts about homes,” he said. “It’s a personal interest that carries through into how I present properties.”.

On setup, agents who play music give similar advice. Keep the volume low enough that buyers can ask questions and the agent can hear their feedback. Use one good speaker rather than several.

Sources indicate that bassova puts hers in the middle of the home, and Seeney puts a small Bluetooth speaker in the kitchen. When sellers have a Sonos system, Daniels connects to it from her MacBook or iPad. Otherwise, she brings her own Bose speaker.

Kilmer runs her music from an iPad instead of her phone. “That way, incoming calls and texts don’t interrupt the music,” she mentioned.

As for proof, none of the agents Inman spoke with track music as a performance metric. Bassova stated she gets buyer feedback that certain homes feel relaxing, but nothing tied to days on market or offers.

In a recent development, so the evidence is anecdotal, and the playlists don’t agree. Agents can’t even settle on jazz. Both camps share one goal: the buyer should notice the home, not the soundtrack.

As Bassova mentioned, “If the buyer begins to think about the music, then it is having a negative impact.”.

Industry News: Tesla on Autopilot/FSD was going 74 mph before fiery crash that killed 3

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A Tesla Model Y left a parkway in El Dorado Hills, California, hit a tree and burst into flames in September, killing three of the four people inside.
  • The crash was widely covered in the Sacramento area as a fiery single-car wreck.
  • Sources indicate that late on Saturday, September 12, 2026, a 2024 Tesla Model Y with four people inside was heading west on Serrano Parkway, between Terracina Drive and Silva Valley Parkway.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A Tesla Model Y left a parkway in El Dorado Hills, California, hit a tree and burst into flames in September, killing three of the four people inside. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators notes Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, with the car doing 74 mph.

The crash was widely covered in the Sacramento area as a fiery single-car wreck. None of that coverage mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data.

Sources indicate that late on Saturday, September 12, 2026, a 2024 Tesla Model Y with four people inside was heading west on Serrano Parkway, between Terracina Drive and Silva Valley Parkway. That’s a residential part of the Serrano community in El Dorado Hills, east of Sacramento.

According to the CHP’s Placerville office, the Model Y left the road “for unknown reasons,” hit a tree on the north side of the parkway, and caught fire. Officers got the call around 10:38 p.m. By the time they arrived, the car was fully engulfed in flames.

It has been revealed that charles Anthony Cameron, 30, of Sacramento, was thrown from the car and died at the scene. Alejandra Mendoza, 28, of Sacramento, and Kailauna Viola Mills, 28, of Roseville, were found dead inside once firefighters put out the fire. One of the two women was driving; CHP hasn’t publicly said which.

It has been revealed that mills lived in Arizona and was visiting family. Her uncle told CBS Sacramento she worked in the medical field and was supposed to get married next April.

A fourth person, a 28-year-old Sacramento woman, survived with major injuries.

CHP indicates the cause is still under investigation. Speed, impairment, and how the car left the road haven’t been released. And nobody has noted a word about Autopilot.

Industry observers note that under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone is killed or hurt. Tesla filed a report on this one.

It lists a 2024 Model Y, a consumer vehicle, and marks the “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That’s Tesla confirming through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 74 mph, a fatality, and the California Highway Patrol as the investigating agency.

Then it redacts the narrative, the software version, and whether the road was inside the system’s operating domain, all as “confidential business information,” the same treatment Tesla gives 99.9% of its reports.

Recent findings suggest that the rest of the report is strangely thin. Tesla lists the roadway type as “Unknown” and what the car hit as “Unknown,” even though police noted it was a tree. It checks only one source for how it learned of the crash: the media. So Tesla found out about a triple-fatal crash in one of its cars from the news, then went into its own data and confirmed its driver-assist was on.

It has been revealed that how we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 05:36 UTC, which is 10:36 p.m. Pacific on September 12, within two minutes of the 10:38 p.m. call CHP responded to. The city, the 2024 Model Y, the month, and the fatal outcome all line up. It’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report from El Dorado Hills in the data. It’s the same crash.

Two of the three victims were found inside the car after the fire was out. The survivor got out of, or was pulled from, the wreckage, depending on the report.

CHP hasn’t noted whether the doors played any role, and we’re not suggesting they did. But it’s a fair question to ask about any Tesla crash with a fire, now that NHTSA is writing new rules for emergency door releases after years of complaints about people getting trapped. We’ve asked.

This is the second triple-fatal crash in Tesla’s latest NHTSA filings where its driver-assist was verified engaged and the public never heard about it. The other one was on I-75 in Naples. Add Vineland and July’s four fatal crashes, and the pattern is hard to miss.

"what little effort went into the report"?

I disagree, a lot of effort went in to minimize the report, to portray it as an unremarkable accident.

That is the effort I find Tesla criminally responsible for.

The CHP need the full report, no redactions. If they chose to censor it that is their task, not Tesla's.

What stands out in this one is how little effort went into the report. Tesla knows the speed, knows the system was on, and has telematics. But it couldn’t fill in what the car hit, and it learned about three deaths in one of its cars from the news. Then it redacted the one field, the narrative, that would tell us what the car did.

Recent findings suggest that tesla wants regulators and customers to trust FSD with no one watching. That trust has to be earned with data. A firm that seals the account of what its car did at 74 mph in a neighborhood, in a crash that killed three people, isn’t earning it.

Industry observers note that we’re asking CHP Placerville whether its investigators knew the system was engaged, whether they got Tesla’s raw data or Tesla’s summary of it, and what they found about the fire and the doors. If CHP never got the full data, how will it ever determine the cause?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that LONDON, Nov.
  • AI is massively accelerating the software delivery lifecycle, and SDLC governance work done by humans no longer scales.
  • Kosli replaces this broken system with automated governance based on cryptographic evidence, allowing teams to deploy changes to production faster, with stronger controls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that LONDON, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kosli today rolled out Control Center, a newly introduced capability that enables enterprise engineering teams to automate SDLC controls at scale.

AI is massively accelerating the software delivery lifecycle, and SDLC governance work done by humans no longer scales. Manual controls cause delays, lead to poor decisions when made under pressure, and can result in non-compliant and insecure changes reaching production.

Kosli replaces this broken system with automated governance based on cryptographic evidence, allowing teams to deploy changes to production faster, with stronger controls.

Control Center is the newest layer in Kosli's Governance Engineering stack for the enterprise, building on the Kosli Evidence Store, which records every event across the SDLC.

With Control Center, teams take the existing controls in their enterprise risk catalogue and define their requirements as code. Kosli evaluates the evidence from the SDLC against those policies in real time, automating control decisions at enterprise scale. Compliant changes can flow to thousands of live applications, while non-compliant changes are stopped at the gate.

Every control decision is recorded alongside the policy and the evidence behind it, so it is easy to reconstruct and explain for audit purposes.

Control Center has been developed in close cooperation with Kosli's existing enterprise customers, and through its work with tier-one financial institutions active in FINOS, where Kosli co-leads the SDLC Controls Framework Working Group. These inputs have enabled Kosli to build an SDLC governance stack that works for any enterprise team.

Recent findings suggest that "It's not uncommon for enterprise teams to build some form of evidence-gathering capability for their SDLC, but that's only the first step to fully automated governance," mentioned Mike Long, CEO of Kosli. "The real challenge is connecting that evidence with the existing controls in your enterprise catalogue. This is what really unlocks the speed and security offered by an AI-assisted SDLC, and it's what we've been able to build thanks to feedback from customers and partners.".

Control Center is in production and available now to all Kosli enterprise customers. Learn more about automating SDLC Governance at scale by visiting kosli.com.

Recent findings suggest that about KosliKosli is governance infrastructure for the AI SDLC, a platform that engineers the controls, evidence and audit trails regulated industries need to ship software at agentic speed without losing compliance. Kosli was founded in 2019 and is backed by Deutsche Bank.

Latest Update: Zoom’s conversations-to-completion strategy is starting to pay off

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1405 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • has spent the better part of the past few years building products to become more than just the video firm everyone used during the pandemic.
  • Total revenue grew 4.9%, but enterprise revenue rose 8.6%, its fastest pace in 13 quarters.
  • The acceleration should be viewed not as a one-quarter anomaly but as a manifestation of the strategy the manufacturer outlined at Zoomtopia about a month ago – moving from “conversations to completion.” That strategy gives customers a reason to buy more of Zoom and builds a competitive moat wider than most investors realize.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 23:43 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

ANALYSIS by Zeus Kerravala.

Zoom Communications Inc. has spent the better part of the past few years building products to become more than just the video firm everyone used during the pandemic. Its fiscal third-quarter results, posted Monday, revealed the strategy is working, though more work remains.

Total revenue grew 4.9%, but enterprise revenue rose 8.6%, its fastest pace in 13 quarters. Zoom raised its full-year outlook and declared its first quarterly dividend of 25 cents per share.

The acceleration should be viewed not as a one-quarter anomaly but as a manifestation of the strategy the manufacturer outlined at Zoomtopia about a month ago – moving from “conversations to completion.” That strategy gives customers a reason to buy more of Zoom and builds a competitive moat wider than most investors realize.

The concept of conversations to completion has enough merit that Microsoft used those exact words at its recent Ignite 2026 event. In fact, it held an entire session on the topic. Though having an 800-pound gorilla like Microsoft jump on a trend might seem threatening, Zoom has a significant lead and can use Microsoft’s marketing to add momentum to its current tailwind.

Nearly all work starts with a conversation: a meeting, a call, a chat thread or a customer interaction. Then everyone leaves, and the real work begins: updating the customer record, writing the follow-up and scheduling the next step. Collaboration vendors have always owned the first step, leaving the second to someone else.

In a recent development, zoom wants both. “We’d like to leverage AI to transform our business from a conversation-centric vendor to a system of completions,” Chief Executive Eric Yuan mentioned on the earnings call. He later put it more plainly: “Conversation is step 1. Step 2, AI will take over.”.

AI agents are swiftly becoming a commodity, and so are the models behind them. What is scarce is context, the knowledge of what was decided, by whom, and why. Zoom sits on the richest source of it in most companies: what people actually mentioned to one another and to customers.

According to recent reports, “Any agent without context really cannot get work done,” Yuan stated. That’s why the unified context layer Zoom showcased at Zoomtopia is central to the story. It links conversations to chats, documents and third-party systems, ensuring people and agents work from the same information.

It has been revealed that my Notes, the company’s AI note-taker, extends that reach to third-party and in-person conversations. Yuan said it is nearing 2 million monthly active customers, with one financial services firm rolling it out to 80,000 wealth advisers. Chief Financial Officer Michelle Chang added that online customers using My Notes have been associated with a 50% reduction in churn.

In a recent development, that is what will create a deeper competitive moat for Zoom. The more context a customer stores with Zoom, the more useful its agents become and the harder it is to leave. Zoom’s moat is not the meeting. Think of it as the memory of the meeting.

A context layer is only as good as the number of conversations it ingests, and this is where Zoom’s breadth of platforms matters. Meetings, phone, chat, contact center and now sales intelligence all feed into the same foundation, and each product gets smarter from the others.

It has been revealed that customers are consolidating. DSI Systems is replacing five separate products with Zoom. SolarWinds expanded its Zoom licenses while “recalibrating its Microsoft package,” according to Yuan. Enterprise net dollar expansion returned to 100%, its highest level in 11 quarters. “Strong RPO growth reflects our continued success in landing larger, longer-term multiproduct platform deals, demonstrating growing demand for our AI-first platform,” Chang said.

Customer experience is where completion gets paid for. Zoom CX recurring revenue grew in the high double digits for the seventh straight quarter, and all 10 of its largest CX deals included paid AI. More telling, Zoom said at Zoomtopia that 90% of its top 100 CX deals in the first half were with customers new to Zoom. Contact center is no longer a cross-sell. It is a front door.

Chang described the differentiation as “the ability to think about customer experience in a whole and fresh upcoming way.” Specifically, she mentioned, “to be able to seamlessly hand off from virtual agents to agents assisted with AI is a significant winner for us.” AI-native startups have the virtual agent but not the human side. Legacy contact center vendors have the humans but not the pace of innovation. Zoom has both on one platform.

In a recent development, there is also an economic moat. Zoom runs most of its AI workload on its own small models and saves the expensive frontier models for harder tasks. “I fundamentally believe no single model can satisfy everything,” Yuan said. Gross margin rose even as AI usage grew, a feat that a point product reselling another manufacturer’s tokens cannot easily match.

The quarter was strong, but analyst questions revealed several concerns.

Recent findings suggest that some will read the dividend as a sign of maturity. With more than $7 billion in cash and free cash flow margins above 40%, I see a manufacturer that can fund innovation and return capital at the same time.

Although these issues came up during the call, most of the investment community remains positive about Zoom. In his note, Arun Bhatia of William Blair wrote, “Churn and downsell rates are becoming more favorable, AI usage and monetization are increasing, and adoption of upcoming products such as Phone and Zoom CX is strong. We are encouraged by these trends and see potential for a growth uptick in the future.”.

Zoom’s headline growth resembles that of a mature software vendor, but the company is in transition, so it’s notable to look beyond the numbers. The underlying enterprise business is built to be a platform that uses context to drive customers toward more products and longer commitments. Investors should watch enterprise growth, net expansion and CX AI attach rates rather than the top line.

For information technology and business leaders, the lesson extends beyond Zoom. Conversation data is a strategic asset, so decide deliberately where it lives and which agents can act on it. Insist on openness so that context can feed the tools you choose. Start where completion is easy to measure, in the contact center and in sales.

According to recent reports, that is where Zoom is proving that the conversation was never the product. The outcome is.

Industry News: Colorado first responders can now get state home mortgage help

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (551 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A borrower earning nearly $197,000 a year usually doesn’t look like a typical candidate for state housing help.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority launched a homeownership program this month for first responders and law enforcement officers.
  • Colorado is among a growing list of states offering homebuying assistance to public-service workers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A borrower earning nearly $197,000 a year usually doesn’t look like a typical candidate for state housing help. In Colorado, if that borrower is a firefighter, emergency medical technician or police officer, the person now qualifies.

Recent findings suggest that the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority launched a homeownership program this month for first responders and law enforcement officers. CHFA Colorado Champions uses a newly introduced state law that raises income limits for eligible borrowers.

Colorado is among a growing list of states offering homebuying assistance to public-service workers. The goal is to give them more chances to live near where they serve. Maryland, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Texas, Florida and South Carolina also offer similar programs.

Earlier this month, Connecticut Gov. Ned Lamont declared a new homeownership assistance program for first responders. It offers up to $25,000 in forgivable down payment and closing cost assistance. The program stems from a law Lamont signed this year.

“By helping reduce one of the biggest barriers to buying a home, we’re investing in the people who serve our state and the communities that depend on them,” Lamont said in a statement.

CHFA Colorado Champions arrives as the housing market weakens, following several years of zoning and regulatory reform.

Colorado’s single-family housing market has been steadily cooling since spring, according to HousingWire Intelligence data through Nov. 20. Inventory peaked in September and has barely eased, while median list prices have fallen since July. Homes are also taking longer to sell, with days on market rising since late July and price reductions staying elevated.

The latest weekly figures show no reversal, with single-family homes taking a median 91 days to sell, up from 84. The median single-family list price is $599,000, and about 48% of single-family listings carry price cuts, the data show.

It has been revealed that lawmakers have spent years trying to improve affordability, mostly by loosening local land-use rules. In 2024, Gov. Jared Polis signed laws requiring more density near transit and clearing the way for accessory dwelling units. The package also removed some parking minimums for urban multifamily housing and lifted limits on unrelated people living together.

A law Polis signed this year requires towns with more than 2,000 people to allow housing on certain small parcels. Eligible land belongs to school districts, colleges, transit districts, housing authorities and qualifying nonprofits. The law takes effect Dec. 31, 2027, while lot-size bills failed in the Legislature this year.

Senate Bill 26-053, a bipartisan law, raised CHFA’s mortgage income limits to 110% of standard guidelines. That allows eligible borrowers earning up to $196,810 a year to qualify.

Recent findings suggest that the program offers a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage. The program covers down payment and closing costs up to the lesser of $25,000 or 4% of the first mortgage. Borrowers apply through a CHFA participating lender.

The aid is a second mortgage. Repayment is deferred until the term ends, the first mortgage is paid off, or the borrower sells, refinances or moves.

Sources indicate that CHFA Executive Director Thomas Bryan remarked in a statement that first responders keep communities safe. Many can’t afford local homes, he added.

Industry observers note that “They should be able to live where they serve,” Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer, one of the law’s sponsors, said in a statement.

Is the IONIQ 5 next in line for an overhaul? Another mysterious IONIQ 5 test mule was recently caught in a parking garage in South Korea, revealing what’s rumored to be Hyundai’s software-defined vehicle (SDV).

Hyundai is betting heavily on software, AI, autonomous driving, robotics, and more as it expands from a traditional auto manufacturer to a “software-centric mobility leader.”.

At the heart of it all is Hyundai Motor Group’s fresh Pleos Connect, an advanced in-vehicle infotainment and software platform.
